+
+/**
+ * The list the grid shows: a group row for each group, then its groups or its data rows when it is
+ * open, and a detail row right after each data row whose key is in `expandedRows` and that has a detail.
+ * Each data row is the keyed object itself. `previous` is the list made the last time: a group row whose
+ * group, state and place are the same, and a detail row whose row and level are, are given back as they
+ * were, so opening one group makes one new group row and draws it and the rows that come or go. With
+ * nothing new the list itself is given back, and without a tree or a detail to add, the keyed rows.
+ */
+export function flattenTree<TRow>(
+  { tree, keyed, expanded, expandedRows, hasDetail }: FlattenInput<TRow>,
+  previous?: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[],
+): readonly FlatRow<TRow>[] {
+  const withDetails = hasDetail !== undefined && expandedRows.size > 0;
+  if (!tree && !withDetails) return keyed;
+
+  let before:
+    | { groups: Map<string, FlatGroupRow<TRow>>; details: Map<DataGridKey, FlatDetailRow<TRow>> }
+    | undefined;
+  const earlier = () => {
+    if (!before) {
+      before = { groups: new Map(), details: new Map() };
+      for (const row of previous ?? []) {
+        if (row.kind === 'group') before.groups.set(row.key, row);
+        else if (row.kind === 'detail') before.details.set(row.key, row);
+      }
+    }
+    return before;
+  };
+
+  const list: FlatRow<TRow>[] = [];
+  const pushData = (row: FlatDataRow<TRow>) => {
+    list.push(row);
+    if (!withDetails || !expandedRows.has(row.key) || !hasDetail(row.row)) return;
+    const was = earlier().details.get(row.key);
+    list.push(
+      was && was.row === row.row && was.level === row.level
+        ? was
+        : { kind: 'detail', key: row.key, row: row.row, level: row.level },
+    );
+  };
+
+  if (!tree) {
+    for (const row of keyed) pushData(row);
+    return list.length === keyed.length ? keyed : settle(list, previous);
+  }
+
+  const except = new Set(expanded.except);
+  // The keyed rows are in the order of the tree, so a walk of it only needs to know how many rows a
+  // group holds to step over the ones a closed group hides.
+  let cursor = 0;
+  const visit = (nodes: readonly GroupNode<TRow>[]) => {
+    nodes.forEach((node, index) => {
+      const open = isGroupOpen({ allExpanded: expanded.allExpanded, except }, node.key);
+      const was = earlier().groups.get(node.key);
+      const setsize = nodes.length;
+      const posinset = index + 1;
+      list.push(
+        was &&
+          was.node === node &&
+          was.expanded === open &&
+          was.setsize === setsize &&
+          was.posinset === posinset

+              kind: 'group',
+              key: node.key,
+              node,
+              level: node.level,
+              expanded: open,
+              setsize,
+              posinset,
+              continued: false,
+            },

+        if (open) visit(node.children);

+        return;
+      }
+      if (open) for (let at = 0; at < node.rows.length; at++) pushData(keyed[cursor + at]!);
+      cursor += node.rows.length;
+    });

+}
+
+// The list just made, or the one before it when every row is the same object in the same order.
+function settle<TRow>(
+  list: FlatRow<TRow>[],
+  previous: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[] | undefined,
+): readonly FlatRow<TRow>[] {
+  return previous && previous.length === list.length && list.every((row, i) => row === previous[i])
+    ? previous
+    : list;
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/engine/group.ts b/src/components/data-grid/engine/group.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..1ae564f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/engine/group.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,218 @@
+import { collator } from '../../../internal/intl';
+import type { DataGridGroupItem } from '../types';
+import { isDataColumn } from './columns';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from './columns';
+import type { TextReader } from './filter';
+import { compareListed, listedValue } from './listing';
+import { computeSummary } from './summary';
+import type { ResolvedSummaryItem, SummaryValues } from './summary';
+import type { Comparable } from './values';
+
+/** One step down the tree: the column grouped by and the value of the group, as the filter holds it. */
+export interface GroupStep {
+  field: string;
+  value: unknown;
+}
+
+/** A group of the tree: the rows that have one value of the level's column, and the groups inside it. */
+export interface GroupNode<TRow> {
+  /** What the state calls the group (`groupKey` of `path`). */
+  key: string;
+  /** The id of the column the level groups by. */
+  field: string;
+  /** From 1, the outermost level. */
+  level: number;
+  /** What the filter holds of the value: `null` for the blank group. */
+  value: unknown;
+  /** The text of the value, as the cells write it. */
+  text: string;
+  path: readonly GroupStep[];
+  /** Every row inside the group, the groups of the levels below included, in the order they came. */
+  rows: readonly TRow[];
+  /** The groups of the next level; `null` at the last level, where `rows` are the leaves. */
+  children: readonly GroupNode<TRow>[] | null;
+  /** The totals of `rows`, when the grouping was given items to total. */
+  totals: SummaryValues<TRow> | null;
+}
+
+/** Where a data row stands in the tree: what its ARIA says of it, and what a group's toggle needs. */
+export interface RowPlace {
+  /** From 1; the levels of the grouping plus 1. */
+  level: number;
+  /** The keys of the groups it is inside, the outermost first. */
+  groups: readonly string[];
+  /** The rows of its group, and its place among them from 1. */
+  setsize: number;
+  posinset: number;
+}
+
+// A value as text that tells it from another. A value JSON cannot write is written by `String`, so a
+// key never throws.
+export function written(value: unknown): string {
+  try {
+    return JSON.stringify(value, (_key, part: unknown) =>
+      typeof part === 'bigint' ? String(part) : part,
+    );
+  } catch {
+    return String(value);
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * The items that group, in their order. An item whose field is not a column of the caller's (the
+ * columns the grid adds for itself are not), whose column does not allow grouping, whose direction is
+ * not `asc` or `desc`, or whose field came before, is dropped without a word, since a state may come
+ * from the end user's storage (spec phase 6 section 5). The columns are every resolved one: a column
+ * the layout hides groups all the same.
+ */
+export function effectiveGrouping<TRow>(
+  items: readonly DataGridGroupItem[],
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[],
+): DataGridGroupItem[] {
+  const kept: DataGridGroupItem[] = [];
+  for (const item of items) {
+    const column = columns.find((candidate) => candidate.id === item.field);
+    if (!column || !isDataColumn(column) || !column.allowGrouping) continue;
+    if (item.direction !== 'asc' && item.direction !== 'desc') continue;
+    if (kept.some((other) => other.field === item.field)) continue;
+    kept.push({ field: item.field, direction: item.direction });
+  }
+  return kept;
+}
+
+/**
+ * What the state calls a group: the JSON of its `[field, value]` steps from the outermost level, the
+ * value being the one the filter holds (an ISO day for a date and a datetime, a lookup's raw value,
+ * `null` for the blank). A key holds the levels above it, so the same value under two parents is two
+ * groups, and a level that is added or moved makes keys that match none of the old ones.
+ */
+export function groupKey(path: readonly GroupStep[]): string {
+  return written(path.map((step) => [step.field, step.value]));
+}
+
+interface Level<TRow> {
+  item: DataGridGroupItem;
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>;
+}
+
+interface Pending<TRow> {
+  value: unknown;
+  text: string;
+  sortKey: Comparable;
+  rows: TRow[];
+  /** The place of first appearance, which breaks a tie. */
+  first: number;
+}
+
+function groupLevel<TRow>(
+  rows: readonly TRow[],
+  levels: readonly Level<TRow>[],
+  depth: number,
+  parent: readonly GroupStep[],
+  read: TextReader<TRow>,
+  compareText: (a: string, b: string) => number,
+  items: readonly ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[] | undefined,
+): GroupNode<TRow>[] {
+  const { item, column } = levels[depth]!;
+  const found = new Map<unknown, Pending<TRow>>();
+  for (const row of rows) {
+    const key = read.key(row, column);
+    let pending = found.get(key);
+    if (!pending) {
+      const { text, sortKey } = listedValue(row, column, read);
+      pending = { value: key, text, sortKey, rows: [], first: found.size };
+      found.set(key, pending);
+    }
+    pending.rows.push(row);
+  }
+  const sign = item.direction === 'asc' ? 1 : -1;
+  const ordered = [...found.values()].sort((a, b) => {
+    // The blank group, and a value with nothing to order it by, come last whichever way the level
+    // goes: a direction turns the values, not where "none" stands.
+    if (a.value === null || b.value === null)
+      return a.value === b.value ? 0 : a.value === null ? 1 : -1;
+    if (a.sortKey === null || b.sortKey === null) {
+      return a.sortKey === b.sortKey ? a.first - b.first : a.sortKey === null ? 1 : -1;
+    }
+    return compareListed(a.sortKey, b.sortKey, compareText) * sign || a.first - b.first;
+  });
+  return ordered.map((pending) => {
+    const path = [...parent, { field: item.field, value: pending.value }];
+    return {
+      key: groupKey(path),
+      field: item.field,
+      level: depth + 1,
+      value: pending.value,
+      text: pending.text,
+      path,
+      rows: pending.rows,
+      children:
+        depth + 1 < levels.length
+          ? groupLevel(pending.rows, levels, depth + 1, path, read, compareText, items)
+          : null,
+      totals: items ? computeSummary(pending.rows, items) : null,
+    };
+  });
+}
+
+/**
+ * The rows as a tree of groups, one level for each item that groups (`effectiveGrouping`: the rest is
+ * ignored). One pass over the rows for each level, with a `Map` by value, so the cost is the rows
+ * times the levels. The groups of a level come in the item's direction, the values ordered as the
+ * header filter's list orders them (`listedValue`); the blank group is last, and values ordered the
+ * same keep the order they first appear in. The rows of a group keep their order, which is the sort's.
+ * With `items` each group carries the totals of its rows. No level that groups: no tree.
+ */
+export function groupRows<TRow>(
+  rows: readonly TRow[],
+  grouping: readonly DataGridGroupItem[],
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[],
+  read: TextReader<TRow>,
+  locale: string,
+  items?: readonly ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[],
+): readonly GroupNode<TRow>[] {
+  const levels: Level<TRow>[] = effectiveGrouping(grouping, columns).map((item) => ({
+    item,
+    column: columns.find((candidate) => candidate.id === item.field)!,
+  }));
+  if (levels.length === 0) return [];
+  const compareText = collator(locale, { numeric: true }).compare;
+  return groupLevel(rows, levels, 0, [], read, compareText, items);
+}
+
+/** The data rows in the order the tree shows them: the leaves, in group order. */
+export function groupedRows<TRow>(tree: readonly GroupNode<TRow>[]): TRow[] {
+  const rows: TRow[] = [];
+  const visit = (nodes: readonly GroupNode<TRow>[]) => {
+    for (const node of nodes) {
+      if (node.children) visit(node.children);
+      else for (const row of node.rows) rows.push(row);
+    }
+  };
+  visit(tree);
+  return rows;
+}
+
+/** The place of each row of `groupedRows(tree)`, in the same order. */
+export function rowPlaces<TRow>(tree: readonly GroupNode<TRow>[]): RowPlace[] {
+  const places: RowPlace[] = [];
+  const visit = (nodes: readonly GroupNode<TRow>[], groups: readonly string[]) => {
+    for (const node of nodes) {
+      const inside = [...groups, node.key];
+      if (node.children) {
+        visit(node.children, inside);
+        continue;
+      }
+      node.rows.forEach((_row, index) => {
+        places.push({
+          level: node.level + 1,
+          groups: inside,
+          setsize: node.rows.length,
+          posinset: index + 1,
+        });
+      });
+    }
+  };
+  visit(tree, []);
+  return places;
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/engine/listing.ts b/src/components/data-grid/engine/listing.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..3693aac
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/engine/listing.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+import { isIsoDate } from '../../../internal/date';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from './columns';
+import type { TextReader } from './filter';
+import { compareKeys } from './sort';
+import type { Comparable } from './values';
+
+/**
+ * One value of a column as a list of values writes it: the header filter's list and the groups of a
+ * grouping both list the values of a column, so they read each value this one way.
+ */
+export interface ListedValue {
+  /** What the filter holds of the value: `null` for a blank (see `filterKey` of the column). */
+  key: unknown;
+  text: string;
+  /** What the value is ordered by; `null` is a blank, which comes last. */
+  sortKey: Comparable;
+}
+
+/**
+ * What a value that no row holds is ordered by, as the column orders its rows: a lookup by its text, a
+ * day by its time, a number as a number. A column with a `sortValue` may order the rows another way; a
+ * value with no row cannot follow it.
+ */
+export function keySortKey<TRow>(
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+  key: unknown,
+  text: string,
+): Comparable {
+  if (column.choices) return text === '' ? null : text;
+  if (typeof key === 'number') return key;
+  if (typeof key === 'boolean') return Number(key);
+  if (isIsoDate(key)) return Date.parse(`${key}T00:00:00Z`);
+  return typeof key === 'string' ? key : null;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The value of `row` in `column` as a list writes it. The key is the one the filter holds, read from
+ * the cache (a datetime's day in the zone its cells are shown in). The text is the cell's, but a
+ * datetime is listed by its day, so its text is that day's, and an empty text is the key as the column
+ * writes it. The order is the column's `sortKey` of the row, so a `sortValue` orders the values and a
+ * lookup is ordered by its text; a datetime's is its day, since a list of days cannot follow the
+ * instants of a `sortValue`.
+ */
+export function listedValue<TRow>(
+  row: TRow,
+  column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>,
+  read: TextReader<TRow>,
+): ListedValue {
+  const key = read.key(row, column);
+  const isDatetime = column.dataType === 'datetime';
+  let text = isDatetime ? '' : read.text(row, column);
+  if (text === '') text = column.keyText(key);
+  return { key, text, sortKey: isDatetime ? keySortKey(column, key, text) : column.sortKey(row) };
+}
+
+/**
+ * Orders two sort keys of listed values: numbers before strings, as the sort does, and a blank after
+ * every other value. Two equal keys are 0: the caller breaks the tie by the place of first appearance.
+ */
+export function compareListed(
+  a: Comparable,
+  b: Comparable,
+  compareText: (a: string, b: string) => number,
+): number {
+  if (a === null || b === null) return a === b ? 0 : a === null ? 1 : -1;
+  return compareKeys(a, b, compareText);
+}

-/** The rows of the page, cut from the whole flat list; a page out of range is the nearest one. */
+// The rows a page counts: data rows and group rows. A detail row belongs to its master, and the repeat
+// of a group at the top of a page (`continued`) to the group it repeats.
+function isCounted<TRow>(row: FlatRow<TRow>): boolean {
+  return row.kind === 'data' || (row.kind === 'group' && !row.continued);
+}
+
+/** The number of rows the pager counts in a list: its data rows and its group rows. */
+export function countRows<TRow>(flat: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[]): number {
+  let count = 0;
+  for (const row of flat) if (isCounted(row)) count++;
+  return count;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The rows of the page, cut from the whole flat list by the rows it counts (`countRows`); a page out
+ * of range is the nearest one. A detail row stays with its master, so a page may show `size` counted
+ * rows and their details. A page that starts inside a group, on a row or on a group row of a deeper
+ * level, starts with the groups it is inside, outermost first, as new rows marked `continued`: the
+ * same groups, with the same order and place, so a reader of the page knows where it is.
+ */
 export function pageRows<TRow>(
   flat: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[],
   page: DataGridPage,
 ): FlatRow<TRow>[] {
   const size = wholeSize(page.size);
   if (size === Infinity) return flat.slice();
-  const start = clampPageIndex(page.index, flat.length, size) * size;
-  return flat.slice(start, start + size);
+  const first = clampPageIndex(page.index, countRows(flat), size) * size;
+  let counted = 0;
+  let from = -1;
+  let to = flat.length;
+  for (let at = 0; at < flat.length; at++) {
+    if (!isCounted(flat[at]!)) continue;
+    if (counted === first) from = at;
+    if (counted === first + size) {
+      to = at;
+      break;
+    }
+    counted++;
+  }
+  if (from < 0) return [];
+
+  const head = flat[from]!;
+  const above: FlatRow<TRow>[] = [];
+  // The groups above the first row are the nearest ones of each level before it.
+  let wanted = head.level - 1;
+  for (let at = from - 1; at >= 0 && wanted > 0; at--) {
+    const row = flat[at]!;
+    if (row.kind === 'group' && row.level === wanted) {
+      above.unshift({ ...row, continued: true });
+      wanted--;
+    }
+  }
+  return [...above, ...flat.slice(from, to)];
 }

+import { numberFormat } from '../../../internal/intl';
+import { isNumber } from '../../../internal/number';
+import type { DataGridSummaryItem } from '../types';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from './columns';
+import { isDataColumn } from './columns';
+import type { TextReader } from './filter';
+import { toComparable } from './values';
+
+const NAMED_TYPES: readonly string[] = ['count', 'sum', 'avg', 'min', 'max'];
+
+/** A total as the engine works with it: the column it shows in and the column it reads, found. */
+export interface ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow> {
+  /** What the item is known by: the caller's `id`, else the type and the field. */
+  readonly id: string;
+  /** The id of the column the total is shown under. */
+  readonly column: string;
+  /** The column the values are read from. */
+  readonly source: ResolvedColumn<TRow>;
+  readonly type: DataGridSummaryItem<TRow>['type'];
+  readonly label: string | undefined;
+  readonly format: DataGridSummaryItem<TRow>['format'];
+}
+
+/**
+ * One total: the value, and for a least or greatest the row that holds it (its text is that row's).
+ * `null` is a blank: the average, least or greatest of no number.
+ */
+export interface SummaryEntry<TRow> {
+  readonly value: unknown;
+  readonly row: TRow | undefined;
+}
+
+/** The totals of a set of rows, each under the id of its item. */
+export type SummaryValues<TRow> = ReadonlyMap<string, SummaryEntry<TRow>>;
+
+/**
+ * The items as the engine reads them. An item that does not name a column of the grid (the one it
+ * shows in, and the one it reads), or whose type is not one of the five or a function, is left out and
+ * handed back in `leftOut`, so the grid can warn once after the commit: this function is pure. An `id`
+ * the caller gives twice is the caller's to keep apart; the later item wins in the values.
+ */
+export function resolveSummaryItems<TRow>(
+  items: readonly DataGridSummaryItem<TRow>[],
+  columns: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[],
+): { items: ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[]; leftOut: DataGridSummaryItem<TRow>[] } {
+  const resolved: ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[] = [];
+  const leftOut: DataGridSummaryItem<TRow>[] = [];
+  for (const item of items) {
+    const field = item.field ?? item.column;
+    const shownIn = columns.find((candidate) => candidate.id === item.column);
+    const source = columns.find((candidate) => candidate.id === field);
+    const named = typeof item.type === 'function' || NAMED_TYPES.includes(item.type);
+    if (!shownIn || !source || !isDataColumn(source) || !named) {
+      leftOut.push(item);
+      continue;
+    }
+    const kind = typeof item.type === 'function' ? 'custom' : item.type;
+    resolved.push({
+      id: typeof item.id === 'string' && item.id !== '' ? item.id : `${kind}:${field}`,
+      column: item.column,
+      source,
+      type: item.type,
+      label: item.label,
+      format: item.format,
+    });
+  }
+  return { items: resolved, leftOut };
+}
+
+// What one item gathers while the rows go by.
+interface Gathered<TRow> {
+  sum: number;
+  numbers: number;
+  best: number | null;
+  bestRow: TRow | undefined;
+}
+
+// A value a least or a greatest can be of: a number, a date or a datetime, as a number to compare.
+function comparableOf<TRow>(row: TRow, source: ResolvedColumn<TRow>): number | null {
+  if (
+    source.dataType !== 'number' &&
+    source.dataType !== 'date' &&
+    source.dataType !== 'datetime'
+  ) {
+    return null;
+  }
+  const comparable = toComparable(source.value(row), source.dataType);
+  return typeof comparable === 'number' ? comparable : null;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The totals of `rows`, one pass for all the items. `count` is the number of rows. `sum` and `avg` read the
+ * finite numbers of the item's field and skip the rest: the sum of none is 0, the average of none is
+ * blank. `min` and `max` read the numbers, dates and datetimes of a column of those types and keep the
+ * row that holds the value (the first, when two do), blank when there is none. A function type is called
+ * once with the rows, and its result is the value.
+ */
+export function computeSummary<TRow>(
+  rows: readonly TRow[],
+  items: readonly ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>[],
+): SummaryValues<TRow> {
+  const gathered = items.map((): Gathered<TRow> => ({
+    sum: 0,
+    numbers: 0,
+    best: null,
+    bestRow: undefined,
+  }));
+  for (const row of rows) {
+    items.forEach((item, index) => {
+      const now = gathered[index]!;
+      switch (item.type) {
+        case 'sum':
+        case 'avg': {
+          const value = item.source.value(row);
+          if (isNumber(value)) {
+            now.sum += value;
+            now.numbers++;
+          }
+          break;
+        }
+        case 'min':
+        case 'max': {
+          const value = comparableOf(row, item.source);
+          if (value === null) break;
+          if (now.best === null || (item.type === 'min' ? value < now.best : value > now.best)) {
+            now.best = value;
+            now.bestRow = row;
+          }
+          break;
+        }
+      }
+    });
+  }
+  const values = new Map<string, SummaryEntry<TRow>>();
+  items.forEach((item, index) => {
+    const now = gathered[index]!;
+    let entry: SummaryEntry<TRow>;
+    if (typeof item.type === 'function') {
+      entry = { value: item.type(rows), row: undefined };
+    } else {
+      switch (item.type) {
+        case 'count':
+          entry = { value: rows.length, row: undefined };
+          break;
+        case 'sum':
+          entry = { value: now.sum, row: undefined };
+          break;
+        case 'avg':
+          entry = { value: now.numbers === 0 ? null : now.sum / now.numbers, row: undefined };
+          break;
+        default:
+          entry = { value: now.best, row: now.bestRow };
+      }
+    }
+    values.set(item.id, entry);
+  });
+  return values;
+}
+
+// A value written by the item's `format`: a function writes it, Intl options write a number, and a
+// set of options Intl refuses writes it as the locale does, since a bad option never throws here.
+function writeValue(
+  value: unknown,
+  format: NonNullable<ResolvedSummaryItem<unknown>['format']>,
+  locale: string,
+) {
+  if (typeof format === 'function') return format(value);
+  if (!isNumber(value)) return String(value);
+  try {
+    return numberFormat(locale, format).format(value);
+  } catch {
+    return numberFormat(locale).format(value);
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * The text of a total. A `count` is a whole number. Otherwise the `format` of the item writes the value
+ * when it has one; without it a `min` or `max` is the text of the row that holds it (so a column's format
+ * function and its Intl options both write it, as in the cells), and a `sum` or `avg` is written as the
+ * column writes a number (its Intl options when it has them) or as the locale does; a function type's
+ * value is written as a string. A blank is the empty text.
+ */
+export function summaryText<TRow>(
+  item: ResolvedSummaryItem<TRow>,
+  entry: SummaryEntry<TRow> | undefined,
+  { locale, read }: { locale: string; read: TextReader<TRow> },
+): string {
+  if (!entry || entry.value === null || entry.value === undefined) return '';
+  const { value } = entry;
+  if (item.type === 'count') {
+    return numberFormat(locale, { maximumFractionDigits: 0 }).format(value as number);
+  }
+  if (item.format !== undefined) return writeValue(value, item.format, locale);
+  if (item.type === 'min' || item.type === 'max') {
+    return entry.row === undefined ? '' : read.text(entry.row, item.source);
+  }
+  if ((item.type === 'sum' || item.type === 'avg') && isNumber(value)) {
+    const { source } = item;
+    // `keyText` writes a number with the column's own Intl options; a lookup writes its items instead.
+    return source.dataType === 'number' && !source.choices
+      ? source.keyText(value)
+      : numberFormat(locale).format(value);
+  }
+  return String(value);
+}

+// Grouping (spec phase 6 §3.5 step 6, §3.6 "Treegrid", §4.3 R1 "Hàng nhóm", §6.3 "Nhóm", "Mở/đóng"): the
+// grouping and the open groups as state, the group rows and the indent columns, the columns a grouping
+// takes out, the keys of a group row, and what choosing and paging do with rows of three kinds.
+
+let showing: Set<Element>;
+beforeEach(() => {
+  resetDevWarnings();
+  showing = new Set();
+  // jsdom has no layout, so every element would count as hidden to the code that looks for the
+  // controls of a cell, and no Popover API: a popover (the chooser's) shows and hides by these stand-ins.
+  HTMLElement.prototype.checkVisibility = () => true;
+  HTMLElement.prototype.showPopover = function showPopover(this: HTMLElement) {
+    showing.add(this);
+  };
+  HTMLElement.prototype.hidePopover = function hidePopover(this: HTMLElement) {
+    showing.delete(this);
+  };
+  const matches = Element.prototype.matches;
+  vi.spyOn(Element.prototype, 'matches').mockImplementation(function (
+    this: Element,
+    selector: string,
+  ) {
+    return selector === ':popover-open' ? showing.has(this) : matches.call(this, selector);
+  });
+});
+afterEach(() => {
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'checkVisibility');
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'showPopover');
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, 'hidePopover');
+  Reflect.deleteProperty(Element.prototype, 'scrollIntoView');
+  vi.restoreAllMocks();
+});

+// Grouping (phase 6 Plan E): a toggle of a group draws that group's row and the rows that come or go,

+describe('the groups', () => {

+  const grouped = (props: Partial<React.ComponentProps<typeof DataGrid<Task>>> = {}) => (
+    <DataGrid
+      data={TASKS}
+      rowKey="id"
+      columns={TASK_COLUMNS}
+      caption="Tasks"
+      paging={false}
+      grouping={BY_TEAM}
+      {...props}
+    />
+  );
+  const reset = () => {
+    renders.cell = 0;
+    renders.headerCell = 0;
+    renders.toolbar = 0;
+    renders.body = 0;
+    groupRenders.groupRow = 0;
+  };
+  const header = (team: string) =>

+    expect(groupRenders.groupRow).toBe(1);
+    expect(renders.cell).toBe(0);
+    expect(renders.headerCell).toBe(0);
+    reset();
+    fireEvent.click(header('B'));
+    // The four that come draw their 3 cells (Team is grouped, so it is no column of the rows).
+    expect(groupRenders.groupRow).toBe(1);
+    expect(renders.cell).toBe(4 * 3);
+    expect(renders.headerCell).toBe(0);
+  });
+
+  it('draws no row for a grouping, open groups and a filter written inline that say what they said', () => {
+    const props = () => ({
+      grouping: [...BY_TEAM],
+      expandedGroups: { allExpanded: true, except: [teamKey('Z')] },

+    reset();
+    rerender(grouped(props()));

+    expect(groupRenders.groupRow).toBe(0);
+    expect(renders.headerCell).toBe(0);
+  });
+});

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/DataGridGrouping.stories.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/DataGridGrouping.stories.tsx
new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/DataGridGrouping.stories.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,424 @@
+import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite';
+import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
+import { expect, userEvent, waitFor, within } from 'storybook/test';
+import { onPlatform } from '../../../.storybook/platform';
+import { realUserEvent } from '../../../.storybook/real-input';
+import { DataGrid } from './DataGrid';
+import type { DataGridColumn, DataGridGroupItem, DataGridProps } from './index';
+
+/**
+ * The orders of R1 (spec phase 6 §4.3 R1, mockup question R): twelve orders in four statuses, whose
+ * group totals are the mockup's. Delivered: four orders, 65.720.000 ₫. Cancelled: one, 890.000 ₫.
+ * Processing: four (DH-1028 and DH-1024 are the mockup's own two, and two of Võ Thị Lan's, 11.350.000 ₫
+ * together). New: three, 55.700.000 ₫. The quantities add to 135, as the mockup's footer says; the
+ * totals add to 162.010.000 ₫, which the mockup's own footer does not (Claude's ruling on OQ 2).
+ */
+interface R1Order {
+  id: string;
+  customer: string;
+  date: string;
+  channel: 'Store' | 'Website' | 'Phone';
+  qty: number;
+  total: number;
+  status: 'Delivered' | 'Cancelled' | 'Processing' | 'New';
+  assignee: string;
+}
+
+const order = (
+  id: string,
+  customer: string,
+  date: string,
+  channel: R1Order['channel'],
+  qty: number,
+  total: number,
+  status: R1Order['status'],
+  assignee: string,
+): R1Order => ({ id, customer, date, channel, qty, total, status, assignee });
+
+const R1_ORDERS: readonly R1Order[] = [
+  order(
+    'DH-1034',
+    'Nhà hàng Sen Vàng',
+    '2026-11-10',
+    'Store',
+    12,
+    21600000,
+    'Delivered',
+    'Lê Quang Huy',
+  ),
+  order(
+    'DH-1031',
+    'Đỗ Khánh Linh',
+    '2026-11-08',
+    'Website',
+    8,
+    14320000,
+    'Delivered',
+    'Lê Quang Huy',
+  ),
+  order(
+    'DH-1030',
+    'Quán Cà phê Mộc',
+    '2026-11-07',
+    'Phone',
+    15,
+    17800000,
+    'Delivered',
+    'Võ Thị Lan',
+  ),
+  order('DH-1027', 'Tiệm Hoa Sen', '2026-11-04', 'Store', 10, 12000000, 'Delivered', 'Võ Thị Lan'),
+  order(
+    'DH-1022',
+    'Công ty Bình Minh',
+    '2026-11-02',
+    'Website',
+    3,
+    890000,
+    'Cancelled',
+    'Nguyễn Minh Anh',
+  ),
+  order(
+    'DH-1028',
+    'Cà phê Sương Sớm',
+    '2026-11-05',
+    'Website',
+    25,
+    9750000,
+    'Processing',
+    'Lê Quang Huy',
+  ),
+  order(
+    'DH-1024',
+    'Công ty Minh Phát',
+    '2026-11-03',
+    'Website',
+    12,
+    18600000,
+    'Processing',
+    'Nguyễn Minh Anh',
+  ),
+  order(
+    'DH-1032',
+    'Studio Ánh Dương',
+    '2026-11-09',
+    'Store',
+    10,
+    6100000,
+    'Processing',
+    'Võ Thị Lan',
+  ),
+  order(
+    'DH-1033',
+    'Công ty An Phát',
+    '2026-11-10',
+    'Phone',
+    8,
+    5250000,
+    'Processing',
+    'Võ Thị Lan',
+  ),
+  order('DH-1035', 'Tạp hóa Hoa Mai', '2026-11-11', 'Website', 14, 22500000, 'New', 'Võ Thị Lan'),
+  order(
+    'DH-1036',
+    'Nhà sách Kim Đồng',
+    '2026-11-11',
+    'Store',
+    9,
+    18200000,
+    'New',
+    'Nguyễn Minh Anh',
+  ),
+  order('DH-1037', 'Cửa hàng Mai Linh', '2026-11-12', 'Phone', 9, 15000000, 'New', 'Lê Quang Huy'),
+];
+
+/** The order R1 lists its statuses in; a column's `sortValue` makes the groups come so. */
+const STATUS_ORDER: readonly R1Order['status'][] = ['Delivered', 'Cancelled', 'Processing', 'New'];
+
+/** E's columns for R1: Order, Customer, Order date, Channel, Qty, Total, then Status and Assignee. */
+const R1_COLUMNS: DataGridColumn<R1Order>[] = [
+  { field: 'id', caption: 'Order', rowHeader: true, width: 120 },
+  { field: 'customer', caption: 'Customer' },
+  { field: 'date', caption: 'Order date', dataType: 'date', width: 150 },
+  { field: 'channel', caption: 'Channel', width: 150 },
+  { field: 'qty', caption: 'Qty', dataType: 'number', width: 110 },
+  {
+    field: 'total',
+    caption: 'Total',
+    dataType: 'number',
+    format: { style: 'currency', currency: 'VND' },
+    width: 200,
+  },
+  {
+    field: 'status',
+    caption: 'Status',
+    width: 140,
+    sortValue: (row) => STATUS_ORDER.indexOf(row.status),
+  },
+  { field: 'assignee', caption: 'Assignee', width: 160 },
+];
+
+const meta = {
+  title: 'Components/DataGrid/Grouping',
+  component: DataGrid,
+  // Built but not released until the grid is exported (spec phase 6 §2): hidden from the sidebar of
+  // the built docs, still run by the story tests and shot by the visual harness.
+  tags: ['unreleased'],
+  args: { data: R1_ORDERS, rowKey: 'id', columns: R1_COLUMNS, 'aria-label': 'Orders' },
+  parameters: {
+    a11y: {
+      config: {
+        rules: [{ id: 'region', enabled: false }],
+      },
+    },
+  },
+} satisfies Meta<DataGridProps<R1Order>>;
+
+export default meta;
+type Story = StoryObj<DataGridProps<R1Order>>;
+
+/**
+ * How long a story waits for the grid to show what a press asked of it: the state changes in the
+ * press, and the commit and the focus it gives come in the engine's next rendering update, which
+ * Linux WebKit on x86 (CI) delivers late. `waitFor` waits one second by default; a late update came
+ * within five. Each message says what was missing, so a late update can be told from one that never
+ * came.
+ */
+const RENDER_UPDATE = { timeout: 5000 };
+
+const BY_STATUS_THEN_ASSIGNEE: DataGridGroupItem[] = [
+  { field: 'status', direction: 'asc' },
+  { field: 'assignee', direction: 'asc' },
+];
+
+const tableOf = (root: HTMLElement) =>
+  root.querySelector<HTMLTableElement>('table[role="grid"], table[role="treegrid"]')!;
+const bodyRowsOf = (root: HTMLElement) =>
+  Array.from(root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tbody > tr'));
+const groupRowsOf = (root: HTMLElement) =>
+  Array.from(root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tbody > tr.flg-data-grid-group-row'));
+
+/**
+ * The inner shadows of an element as `[x, y]` offsets: the computed `box-shadow` writes each as four
+ * lengths (x, y, blur, spread) next to its colour, whatever the engine's order of the parts.
+ */
+const insetOffsets = (element: HTMLElement): Array<[number, number]> => {
+  const shadow = getComputedStyle(element).boxShadow;
+  if (shadow === 'none') return [];
+  const lengths = /(-?[\d.]+)px (-?[\d.]+)px (-?[\d.]+)px (-?[\d.]+)px/g;
+  return Array.from(shadow.matchAll(lengths), (match) => [Number(match[1]), Number(match[2])]);
+};
+const hasInset = (element: HTMLElement, x: number, y: number) =>
+  insetOffsets(element).some(([dx, dy]) => dx === x && dy === y);
+
+/** A grid that a key of the story ungroups and groups again, with the focus staying in the grid. */
+const RoleGrid = (props: Partial<DataGridProps<R1Order>>) => {
+  const [grouping, setGrouping] = useState<DataGridGroupItem[]>(BY_STATUS_THEN_ASSIGNEE);
+  const box = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
+  // The `g` key is no key of the grid: it comes to this listener from the cell that has the focus.
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const element = box.current!;
+    const onKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
+      if (event.key === 'g') setGrouping((now) => (now.length > 0 ? [] : BY_STATUS_THEN_ASSIGNEE));
+    };
+    element.addEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);
+    return () => element.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);
+  }, []);
+  return (
+    <div ref={box} style={{ width: 560 }}>
+      <DataGrid
+        aria-label="Orders"
+        data={R1_ORDERS}
+        rowKey="id"
+        columns={R1_COLUMNS}
+        paging={false}
+        grouping={grouping}
+        {...props}
+      />
+    </div>
+  );
+};
+
+/**
+ * The keys of a group row (spec phase 6 §3.6, the tree grid pattern), with real input: Tab lands on
+ * the first group row, the one stop of the grid; → opens a group, or goes to its first row; ← closes
+ * an open group, or goes to the group above; Enter opens it again; Home and End go to the first and
+ * the last row. The row with the focus has a frame of 2px around the whole row, drawn from the inner
+ * shadows of its cells: top and bottom on each cell, the left side on the first, the right side on
+ * the last. A group row that takes the focus scrolls the frame vertically only: a frame scrolled
+ * sideways keeps its `scrollLeft`. Ungrouping a grid, which changes its role, keeps the focus in it.
+ */
+export const GroupRowKeys: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  beforeEach: onPlatform('other'),
+  render: () => <RoleGrid />,
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    const frame = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-frame')!;
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    const table = tableOf(root);
+    await expect(table).toHaveAttribute('role', 'treegrid');
+    await waitFor(() => expect(frame.scrollWidth).toBeGreaterThan(frame.clientWidth + 100));
+    if (!real) return;
+
+    const stops = () => table.querySelectorAll('[tabindex="0"]');
+    const active = () => document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
+    const level = (row: HTMLElement) => row.getAttribute('aria-level');
+    const first = groupRowsOf(root)[0]!;
+    // Tab lands on the first group row, the one stop of the grid.
+    for (let tabs = 0; tabs < 4 && !table.contains(document.activeElement); tabs += 1) {
+      await real.tab();
+    }
+    await expect(active()).toBe(first);
+    await expect(stops()).toHaveLength(1);
+
+    // The frame around the whole row, measured from the shadows of its cells.
+    const cells = Array.from(first.children) as HTMLElement[];
+    await expect(cells.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
+    for (const [at, cell] of cells.entries()) {
+      await expect(hasInset(cell, 0, 2), `cell ${at} has the top side`).toBe(true);
+      await expect(hasInset(cell, 0, -2), `cell ${at} has the bottom side`).toBe(true);
+    }
+    await expect(hasInset(cells[0]!, 2, 0), 'the first cell has the left side').toBe(true);
+    await expect(hasInset(cells.at(-1)!, -2, 0), 'the last cell has the right side').toBe(true);
+
+    // → on an open group goes to its first row, a group of the next level.
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowRight}');
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(level(active()), 'the focus is on a row of level 2').toBe('2'),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    const inner = active();
+    await expect(inner.classList.contains('flg-data-grid-group-row')).toBe(true);
+    // ← closes it (it is open), and then goes up to the group above (it is closed).
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}');
+    await waitFor(() => expect(inner).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false'), RENDER_UPDATE);
+    await expect(active()).toBe(inner);
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}');
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(active(), 'the focus is on the group above').toBe(first),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    // ← closes the open first level, and has nothing above it once closed.
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}');
+    await waitFor(() => expect(first).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false'), RENDER_UPDATE);
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowLeft}');
+    await expect(active()).toBe(first);
+    await expect(first).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
+    // Enter opens it again.
+    await real.keyboard('{Enter}');
+    await waitFor(() => expect(first).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true'), RENDER_UPDATE);
+
+    // End on a group row goes to the last row of the list; Home on a data row goes to its first cell, and
+    // mod+Home to the first row, a group row.
+    await real.keyboard('{End}');
+    await waitFor(() => {
+      const rows = bodyRowsOf(root);
+      expect(active().closest('tr'), 'the focus is on the last row').toBe(rows.at(-1));
+    }, RENDER_UPDATE);
+    await real.keyboard('{Control>}{Home}{/Control}');
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(active(), 'the focus is back on the first row').toBe(first),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(stops()).toHaveLength(1);
+  },
+};
+
+/**
+ * A group row that takes the focus, in a frame scrolled sideways, scrolls the frame vertically only
+ * (spec phase 6 §3.6): the cell with the focus is far to the right, ↑ goes to the row above, which is
+ * as wide as the table, and `scrollLeft` is what it was.
+ */
+export const GroupRowKeepsScrollLeft: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  render: () => <RoleGrid />,
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    const frame = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-frame')!;
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    await waitFor(() => expect(frame.scrollWidth).toBeGreaterThan(frame.clientWidth + 100));
+    if (!real) return;
+    // A press on a cell of the first data row makes it the place; then the frame is scrolled sideways.
+    const cell = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('tbody > tr.flg-data-grid-row [tabindex]')!;
+    await real.click(cell);
+    await waitFor(() => expect(document.activeElement).toBe(cell), RENDER_UPDATE);
+    frame.scrollLeft = 200;
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(frame.scrollLeft, 'the frame is scrolled').toBeGreaterThan(100),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    const left = frame.scrollLeft;
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowUp}');
+    await waitFor(
+      () =>
+        expect(
+          (document.activeElement as HTMLElement).classList.contains('flg-data-grid-group-row'),
+          'the focus is on a group row',
+        ).toBe(true),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(frame.scrollLeft).toBe(left);
+  },
+};
+
+/**
+ * The table is a `grid` and becomes a `treegrid` as the rows are grouped, and back; the focus stays in
+ * the grid across both changes, on a place of it, never on the page.
+ */
+export const RoleChangeKeepsFocus: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  render: () => <RoleGrid />,
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    const cell = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('tbody > tr.flg-data-grid-row [tabindex]')!;
+    await real.click(cell);
+    await waitFor(() => expect(document.activeElement).toBe(cell), RENDER_UPDATE);
+    await real.keyboard('g');
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(tableOf(root), 'the table is a grid').toHaveAttribute('role', 'grid'),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(tableOf(root).contains(document.activeElement)).toBe(true);
+    await real.keyboard('g');
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(tableOf(root), 'the table is a treegrid').toHaveAttribute('role', 'treegrid'),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(tableOf(root).contains(document.activeElement)).toBe(true);
+  },
+};
+
+/**
+ * Pages count the group rows and the data rows of the list: sixteen rows here, six to a page. The
+ * second page starts inside Cancelled, so it begins with that group's row again, "(continued)",
+ * before its own rows; the pager says the rows it counts.
+ */
+export const GroupedPaging: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  args: {
+    grouping: [{ field: 'status', direction: 'asc' }],
+    paging: { pageSize: 6, pageSizes: [6] },
+  },
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const canvas = within(canvasElement);
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    await expect(canvas.getByText('1–6 of 16')).toBeVisible();
+    await expect(bodyRowsOf(root)).toHaveLength(6);
+    await expect(groupRowsOf(root).map((row) => row.textContent)).toEqual([
+      'Status: Delivered (4)',
+      'Status: Cancelled (1)',
+    ]);
+    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole('button', { name: 'Next page' }));
+    await waitFor(() => expect(canvas.getByText('7–12 of 16')).toBeVisible(), RENDER_UPDATE);
+    const rows = bodyRowsOf(root);
+    // The repeat is not a counted row: six counted rows and the repeat make seven.
+    await expect(rows).toHaveLength(7);
+    await expect(rows[0]).toHaveTextContent('Status: Cancelled (1) (continued)');
+    await expect(rows[0]!.classList.contains('flg-data-grid-group-row')).toBe(true);
+    await expect(rows[0]).toHaveAttribute('aria-posinset', '2');
+    await expect(rows[1]).toHaveTextContent('DH-1022');
+    await expect(rows[2]).toHaveTextContent('Status: Processing (4)');
+  },
+};

+// The three kinds of row of the body, and the cells of a row that are places of the keyboard.
+function bodyOf(spec: string[]) {
+  const table = document.createElement('table');
+  const body = table.createTBody();
+  for (const classes of spec) {
+    const row = body.insertRow();
+    if (classes) row.className = classes;
+  }
+  return table;
+}
+
+describe('the kinds of row', () => {
+  const SPEC = [
+    'flg-data-grid-group-row',
+    'flg-data-grid-row',
+    'flg-data-grid-detail-row',
+    'flg-data-grid-spacer',
+    'flg-data-grid-row',
+  ];
+
+  it('are told apart once, by the class of the row; a spacer is none', () => {
+    const rows = Array.from(bodyOf(SPEC).tBodies[0]!.rows);
+    expect(rows.map(rowKind)).toEqual(['group', 'data', 'detail', null, 'data']);
+  });
+
+  it('are all in listRows, in order, and only the data rows in dataRows', () => {
+    const table = bodyOf(SPEC);
+    expect(listRows(table).map(rowKind)).toEqual(['group', 'data', 'detail', 'data']);
+    expect(dataRows(table).map(rowKind)).toEqual(['data', 'data']);
+  });
+
+  it('count every kind in the place of a row, which is its place in the list', () => {
+    const table = bodyOf(SPEC);
+    const [group, data, detail, , last] = Array.from(table.tBodies[0]!.rows);
+    expect(rowAt(table, 0)).toBe(group);
+    expect(rowAt(table, 1)).toBe(data);
+    expect(rowAt(table, 2)).toBe(detail);
+    expect(rowAt(table, 3)).toBe(last);
+    expect(rowAt(table, 4)).toBeUndefined();
+  });
+});
+
+describe('cellsOf', () => {
+  it('leaves out the filler column and the indents of the groups, which are no place of the keyboard', () => {
+    const row = document.createElement('tr');
+    const make = (classes: string) => {
+      const cell = row.insertCell();
+      cell.className = classes;
+      return cell;
+    };
+    make('flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-indent');
+    make('flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-indent');
+    const first = make('flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-cell');
+    make('flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-filler');
+    const last = make('flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-cell');
+    expect(cellsOf(row)).toEqual([first, last]);
+  });
+});
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-grouping.test.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-grouping.test.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..5390254
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-grouping.test.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,205 @@
+import { act, renderHook } from '@testing-library/react';
+import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { resolveColumns } from '../engine/columns';
+import type { DataGridColumn, DataGridExpandedGroups, DataGridState } from '../types';
+import { useGridGrouping } from './use-grid-grouping';
+import { useGridState } from './use-grid-state';
+
+// The grouping, with the state it writes to (`useGridState`) and no grid: the one way the user changes
+// the grouping (`applyGrouping`), the toggle of a group and "open every group" and "close every group".
+
+interface Row {
+  status: string;
+  name: string;
+  locked: string;
+}
+
+const COLUMNS: DataGridColumn<Row>[] = [
+  { field: 'status', caption: 'Status' },
+  { field: 'name', caption: 'Name' },
+  { field: 'locked', caption: 'Locked', allowGrouping: false },
+];
+const RESOLVED = resolveColumns(COLUMNS as DataGridColumn<unknown>[], {
+  locale: 'en-US',
+  timeZone: 'UTC',
+  yes: 'Yes',
+  no: 'No',
+  allowSorting: true,
+  allowResizing: true,
+  allowReordering: true,
+  allowPinning: true,
+  allowHiding: true,
+  allowFiltering: true,
+  allowHeaderFiltering: true,
+  allowGrouping: true,
+});
+const BY_STATUS = [{ field: 'status', direction: 'asc' as const }];
+const BY_NAME = [{ field: 'name', direction: 'asc' as const }];
+const OPEN: DataGridExpandedGroups = { allExpanded: true, except: [] };
+
+function setup({
+  page = 0,
+  remote = false,
+  grouping,
+  onStateChange,
+}: {
+  page?: number;
+  remote?: boolean;
+  grouping?: typeof BY_STATUS;
+  onStateChange?: (state: DataGridState, part: keyof DataGridState) => void;
+} = {}) {
+  const calls: string[] = [];
+  const announce = vi.fn();
+  const shown = {
+    current: {
+      sort: [],
+      filter: {},
+      page: { index: page, size: 5 },
+      selectedKeys: [],
+      columnLayout: { order: [], widths: {}, hidden: [], pinned: {} },
+      grouping: grouping ?? [],
+      expandedGroups: OPEN,
+    } satisfies DataGridState,
+  };
+  const hook = renderHook(() => {
+    const held = useGridState({
+      sort: undefined,
+      defaultSort: undefined,
+      onSortChange: undefined,
+      filter: undefined,
+      defaultFilter: undefined,
+      onFilterChange: undefined,
+      page: undefined,
+      defaultPage: { index: page, size: 5 },
+      onPageChange: (next) => calls.push(`page ${next.index}`),
+      selectedKeys: undefined,
+      defaultSelectedKeys: undefined,
+      onSelectedKeysChange: undefined,
+      columnLayout: undefined,
+      defaultColumnLayout: shown.current.columnLayout,
+      onColumnLayoutChange: undefined,
+      grouping: undefined,
+      defaultGrouping: grouping,
+      onGroupingChange: (next) => calls.push(`grouping ${next.map((item) => item.field)}`),
+      expandedGroups: undefined,
+      defaultExpandedGroups: OPEN,
+      onExpandedGroupsChange: (next) =>
+        calls.push(`expanded ${next.allExpanded} ${next.except.length}`),
+      onStateChange: (state, part) => {
+        calls.push(`state ${part}`);
+        onStateChange?.(state, part);
+      },
+      shown,
+    });
+    const view = useGridGrouping({
+      grouping: held.state.grouping,
+      resolved: RESOLVED,
+      remote,
+      setGrouping: held.setGrouping,
+      setExpandedGroups: held.setExpandedGroups,
+      expandedNow: held.expandedNow,
+      setPage: held.setPage,
+      pageIndex: held.state.page.index,
+      size: 5,
+      paged: true,
+      announce,
+    });
+    return { held, view };
+  });
+  return { ...hook, calls, announce };
+}
+
+describe('which items group', () => {
+  it('are the ones of columns that allow it, in order, and none in server mode', () => {
+    const { result } = setup({
+      grouping: [
+        { field: 'locked', direction: 'asc' },
+        { field: 'nothing', direction: 'asc' },
+        ...BY_STATUS,
+      ],
+    });
+    expect(result.current.view.levels).toEqual(BY_STATUS);
+    expect(result.current.view.fields).toEqual(['status']);
+    expect(setup({ grouping: BY_STATUS, remote: true }).result.current.view.levels).toEqual([]);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('applyGrouping', () => {
+  it('calls onGroupingChange and then onStateChange with the grouping asked, and says what it was given', () => {
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn();
+    const { result, calls, announce } = setup({ onStateChange });
+    act(() => result.current.view.applyGrouping(BY_STATUS, 'Grouped by Status'));
+    expect(calls).toEqual(['grouping status', 'state grouping']);
+    expect(onStateChange.mock.calls[0]![0].grouping).toEqual(BY_STATUS);
+    expect(result.current.held.state.grouping).toEqual(BY_STATUS);
+    expect(announce).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('Grouped by Status');
+  });
+
+  it('goes to the first page as a second change with its own pair, before it says anything', () => {
+    const { result, calls, announce } = setup({ page: 2 });
+    act(() => result.current.view.applyGrouping(BY_STATUS, 'Grouped'));
+    expect(calls).toEqual(['grouping status', 'state grouping', 'page 0', 'state page']);
+    expect(result.current.held.state.page).toEqual({ index: 0, size: 5 });
+    expect(announce).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+  });
+
+  it('does nothing at all for a grouping that says what is held, or what the same event asked', () => {
+    const { result, calls, announce } = setup({ page: 2, grouping: BY_STATUS });
+    act(() => result.current.view.applyGrouping([{ field: 'status', direction: 'asc' }], 'Same'));
+    expect(calls).toEqual([]);
+    expect(announce).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    act(() => {
+      result.current.view.applyGrouping(BY_NAME, 'First');
+      result.current.view.applyGrouping(BY_NAME, 'Second');
+    });
+    expect(calls.filter((call) => call === 'grouping name')).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(announce).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith('First');
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the page when it is the first, and says nothing without a sentence', () => {
+    const { result, calls, announce } = setup();
+    act(() => result.current.view.applyGrouping(BY_NAME));
+    expect(calls).toEqual(['grouping name', 'state grouping']);
+    expect(announce).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+  });
+});
+
+describe('toggleGroup, expandAll and collapseAll', () => {
+  it('closes an open group by listing it, and opens it again by taking it off', () => {
+    const { result, calls } = setup({ grouping: BY_STATUS });
+    act(() => result.current.view.toggleGroup('a'));
+    expect(result.current.held.state.expandedGroups).toEqual({ allExpanded: true, except: ['a'] });
+    act(() => result.current.view.toggleGroup('a'));
+    expect(result.current.held.state.expandedGroups).toEqual(OPEN);
+    expect(calls).toEqual([
+      'expanded true 1',
+      'state expandedGroups',
+      'expanded true 0',
+      'state expandedGroups',
+    ]);
+  });
+
+  it('sees the toggle of an earlier request of the same event', () => {
+    const { result } = setup({ grouping: BY_STATUS });
+    act(() => {
+      result.current.view.toggleGroup('a');
+      result.current.view.toggleGroup('b');
+    });
+    expect(result.current.held.state.expandedGroups).toEqual({
+      allExpanded: true,
+      except: ['a', 'b'],
+    });
+  });
+
+  it('opens and closes every group, and calls nothing when that is what is held', () => {
+    const { result, calls } = setup({ grouping: BY_STATUS });
+    act(() => result.current.view.expandAll());
+    expect(calls).toEqual([]);
+    act(() => result.current.view.collapseAll());
+    expect(calls).toEqual(['expanded false 0', 'state expandedGroups']);
+    act(() => result.current.view.collapseAll());
+    expect(calls).toHaveLength(2);
+    act(() => result.current.view.expandAll());
+    expect(result.current.held.state.expandedGroups).toEqual(OPEN);
+  });
+});

@@ -306,3 +314,87 @@ describe('the filter in useGridState', () => {
     expect(onStateChange.mock.calls[2]![0].filter).toBe(SHOWN.filter);

 });
+
+describe('the grouping and the open groups in useGridState', () => {
+  const BY_A = [{ field: 'a', direction: 'asc' as const }];
+  const BY_B = [{ field: 'b', direction: 'desc' as const }];
+  const CLOSED = { allExpanded: false, except: [] };
+
+  it('start from the defaults and hold what is asked while uncontrolled', () => {
+    const { result } = renderHook(() =>
+      useGridState(options({ defaultGrouping: BY_A, defaultExpandedGroups: CLOSED })),
+    );
+    expect(result.current.state.grouping).toBe(BY_A);
+    expect(result.current.state.expandedGroups).toBe(CLOSED);
+    act(() => void result.current.setGrouping(BY_B));
+    expect(result.current.state.grouping).toBe(BY_B);
+  });
+
+  it('report a grouping to onGroupingChange and then to onStateChange, with the shown state', () => {
+    const calls: string[] = [];
+    const onGroupingChange = vi.fn(() => void calls.push('grouping'));
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn(() => void calls.push('state'));
+    const { result } = renderHook(() => useGridState(options({ onGroupingChange, onStateChange })));
+    let asked = false;
+    act(() => {
+      asked = result.current.setGrouping(BY_A);
+    });
+    expect(asked).toBe(true);
+    expect(calls).toEqual(['grouping', 'state']);
+    expect(onGroupingChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(BY_A);
+    expect(onStateChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith({ ...SHOWN, grouping: BY_A }, 'grouping');
+  });
+
+  it('report the open groups the same way, with the groups that are asked', () => {
+    const calls: string[] = [];
+    const onExpandedGroupsChange = vi.fn(() => void calls.push('expanded'));
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn(() => void calls.push('state'));
+    const { result } = renderHook(() =>
+      useGridState(options({ onExpandedGroupsChange, onStateChange })),
+    );
+    act(() => void result.current.setExpandedGroups(CLOSED));
+    expect(calls).toEqual(['expanded', 'state']);
+    expect(onStateChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith(
+      { ...SHOWN, expandedGroups: CLOSED },
+      'expandedGroups',
+    );
+  });
+
+  it('report nothing for what is held, what an earlier request of the event asked, or the same keys', () => {
+    const onGroupingChange = vi.fn();
+    const onExpandedGroupsChange = vi.fn();
+    const { result } = renderHook(() =>
+      useGridState(options({ defaultGrouping: BY_A, onGroupingChange, onExpandedGroupsChange })),
+    );
+    let first = true;
+    let second = true;
+    act(() => {
+      first = result.current.setGrouping([{ field: 'a', direction: 'asc' }]);
+    });
+    expect([first, onGroupingChange.mock.calls.length]).toEqual([false, 0]);
+    act(() => {
+      result.current.setGrouping(BY_B);
+      second = result.current.setGrouping([{ field: 'b', direction: 'desc' }]);
+    });
+    expect([second, onGroupingChange.mock.calls.length]).toEqual([false, 1]);
+    // The keys of `except` are a set: another order, or a key twice, is no change.
+    act(() => void result.current.setExpandedGroups({ allExpanded: true, except: ['x', 'y'] }));
+    act(
+      () => void result.current.setExpandedGroups({ allExpanded: true, except: ['y', 'x', 'y'] }),
+    );
+    expect(onExpandedGroupsChange).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+  });
+
+  it('send a controlled grouping over what the grid shows, and forget what was asked after the event', async () => {
+    const onStateChange = vi.fn();
+    const { result } = renderHook(() => useGridState(options({ grouping: BY_A, onStateChange })));
+    act(() => {
+      result.current.setGrouping(BY_B);
+      result.current.setPage({ index: 1, size: 20 });
+    });
+    expect(onStateChange.mock.calls[1]![0].grouping).toBe(BY_B);
+    await Promise.resolve();
+    act(() => result.current.setPage({ index: 2, size: 20 }));
+    expect(onStateChange.mock.calls[2]![0].grouping).toBe(SHOWN.grouping);
+  });
+});

 **Cuộn ảo** (`scrolling="virtual"`; bản quyết định):
 
-- **Chiều cao cố định theo loại dòng:** dòng dữ liệu `rowHeight` (theo `density` và `variant`, bảng ở §4.3; ghi đè bằng prop `rowHeight`), hàng nhóm `rowHeight − 8`. Sau khi mount, grid đo khoảng cách thật giữa hai dòng liền nhau (gồm viền 1px của `lined` và `border-spacing` 2px của `striped`) và dùng số đo đó, để engine nào tính viền khác đi cũng không trôi (đo lại khi `density`, `variant` hay `rowHeight` đổi). +- **Chiều cao cố định theo loại dòng:** dòng dữ liệu `rowHeight` (theo `density` và `variant`, bảng ở §4.3; ghi đè bằng prop `rowHeight`), hàng nhóm theo bảng mật độ (chiều cao dòng dữ liệu của `density` và `variant` trừ 8px, không theo prop `rowHeight`, vì `rowHeight` là của dòng dữ liệu; Claude chốt OQ 1, phát hiện khi lập Plan E). Sau khi mount, grid đo khoảng cách thật giữa hai dòng liền nhau (gồm viền 1px của `lined` và `border-spacing` 2px của `striped`) và dùng số đo đó, để engine nào tính viền khác đi cũng không trôi (đo lại khi `density`, `variant` hay `rowHeight` đổi). Trước khi đo: hằng số của bảng §4.3.
 - **Cửa sổ:** các dòng giao với `[scrollTop − vùng đệm, scrollTop + chiều cao khung + vùng đệm]`, vùng đệm 6 dòng mỗi phía; cuộn được cập nhật trong `requestAnimationFrame`. Phần trên và dưới cửa sổ là hai hàng đệm `aria-hidden` cao bằng tổng chiều cao của các dòng không render. Phát hiện khi lập Plan B: hàng đệm cao bằng tổng đó **trừ** khoảng `border-spacing` (2px) mà bảng `striped` thêm quanh mỗi hàng, kể cả hàng đệm (không trừ thì mỗi hàng đệm làm các dòng trôi 2px); khung của lưới ảo có `overflow-anchor: none` (`data-virtual`), vì neo cuộn sẽ tự đổi `scrollTop` khi chiều cao hàng đệm đổi; hàng đệm không có `padding` hay viền của ô, không có lớp `flg-table-row`, và không bao giờ cao 0 (hàng đệm 0px bị bỏ). Cửa sổ chưa có chiều cao khung đo được (lần render đầu, server, jsdom) là `ceil(height / rowHeight) + 6` dòng đầu khi `height` là số, 20 dòng khi không. Cửa sổ là state của `Body` (`useVirtualRows` gọi trong `Body`, tìm bảng và khung từ chính `<tbody>` của nó, vì ref của gốc được gắn sau effect của con lúc mount), không phải của gốc grid: một khung hình cuộn chỉ vẽ lại `Body` và các dòng mới vào, không vẽ lại tiêu đề, thanh công cụ, thanh phân trang, và không chạy effect nào của gốc (nhả control, phím, cuộn chờ); bàn phím và handle hỏi cửa sổ qua một liên kết (`scrollToIndex`, `Body` ghi khi commit), và `Body` báo qua nó sau mỗi lần cửa sổ đổi, để focus mà một phím đang chờ được đưa vào dòng vừa vẽ (phát hiện khi review PR #42), và để focus mà grid đã mất trong một commit chỉ của `Body` được trả về ô hoạt động, như commit của grid làm: focus trong popup của một ô không làm dòng đó thành dòng hoạt động, nên một lần cuộn có thể gỡ dòng đó (vòng sửa thứ hai của review PR #42).
 - **Dòng đang có focus luôn được render** (Claude chốt): nếu dòng hoạt động nằm ngoài cửa sổ trong khi focus ở trong grid (người dùng cuộn bằng chuột), nó được render đúng chỗ của nó, hàng đệm tách làm hai quanh nó. Focus không bao giờ rơi về `<body>` vì dòng của nó bị gỡ. Phát hiện khi lập Plan B: dòng hoạt động được giữ **dù focus có ở trong grid hay không**, vì ô của nó là Tab stop duy nhất (§3.6): bị gỡ khi focus ở ngoài thì Tab đi qua grid mà không dừng ở đâu.

+## Grouping
+
+`grouping` is a list of levels, outermost first: `{ field, direction }`, where `field` is the id of a
+column and `direction` is `'asc'` or `'desc'` (the order of the groups of that level). It is state
+like the sort: `grouping`, `defaultGrouping` and `onGroupingChange`, and `onStateChange` hears it
+as the part `'grouping'`. A grouped grid is a **tree grid**: the table has `role="treegrid"`, and
+each group is a row of its own.
+
+```tsx
+<DataGrid
+  data={orders}
+  rowKey="id"
+  columns={columns}
+  caption="Orders"
+  defaultGrouping={[
+    { field: 'status', direction: 'asc' },
+    { field: 'assignee', direction: 'asc' },
+  ]}
+/>
+```
+
+A **group row** says the name of the column, the value of the group and its number of rows, "Status:
+Delivered (4)", with a chevron that says whether the group is open. The value is written as the
+cells write it (a lookup's text, a formatted number, a day in the grid's `locale` and `timeZone`),
+and a blank value is the group `labels.blank`, which comes last in both directions. The groups of a
+level come in the order of the funnel's list for that column, which is the order the column sorts
+by. A press anywhere on a group row opens or closes it, and a double press does it once. The rows
+inside it are one level deeper: `aria-level` counts the levels of the grouping and one more, and
+`aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` say a row's place in its group.
+
+Each level of the grouping has an **indent column** of 28px after the column of boxes; one cell in
+the heading stands over them all, with the hidden words `labels.groupsAndDetails`. An indent column
+is part of the layout (it has a width and is pinned with the first pinned column) and never a place
+of the keyboard. A column the grid groups by leaves the heading, the rows, the filter row and the
+funnels, since its value is in the group rows: its conditions still filter, it keeps its place, width,
+pin and `hidden` in the layout, and it comes back when the grouping goes. Say `showWhenGrouped: true`
+on a column to keep it in the rows too. If the grouping would leave no column, the first grouped
+column stays. The column chooser lists the columns that are shown only, and the filter panel says the
+conditions of a grouped column after the shown ones, in the order of the grouping, before the hidden
+ones. A grouped column is searched as if it was shown, and its group rows mark a match in the value.
+
+### Open and closed
+
+`expandedGroups` says which groups are open: `{ allExpanded, except }`. With `allExpanded: true`
+every group is open but the ones in `except`; with `false` every group is closed but the ones in
+`except`. It is state too: `expandedGroups`, `defaultExpandedGroups` and `onExpandedGroupsChange`,
+and `onStateChange` hears the part `'expandedGroups'`. Groups start open; `autoExpandAll={false}`
+starts them closed, and `defaultExpandedGroups` wins over it. `autoExpandAll` is read once, as a
+default is. `ref.current.expandAllGroups()` and `ref.current.collapseAllGroups()` open and close
+every group, and call nothing when that is what is held.
+
+A **group key** is the JSON text of the `[field, value]` steps from the outermost level down to the
+group, the value being the one the filter holds for the column: a day as `YYYY-MM-DD` for a `date`
+and a `datetime` (in the grid's `timeZone`), a lookup's raw value, `null` for the blank group. A key
+holds the levels above it, so the same value under two parents is two groups. A key that no group
+has is ignored and stays in the state, as does an item of `grouping` that names no column, a
+column that does not allow grouping or a field that came before: they group nothing and say nothing,
+since a state from a person's storage may hold them. A column that comes after the mount groups when
+it arrives, if `defaultGrouping` names it. A `grouping` that is not an array, or an item that is not
+an object, warns once and the rest is kept.
+
+### Pages, choosing and server mode
+
+The pager counts the group rows and the data rows: "1–20 of 52" counts both. A page may start inside
+a group; it then begins with that group's row again, with `labels.continued` after it, and that row
+is the group's own (it opens and closes it). A change of the grouping goes to the first page, which
+calls `onPageChange` once more when the page was not the first; a press that opens or closes a group
+keeps the page. A group row has no box. "Select all" chooses the data rows of the page, or every row
+after the filter with `selectAllMode="all"`, the rows of closed groups too; a range from Shift
+is taken over the data rows that are shown, so the rows of a closed group are left out of it.
+
+With `remote` the grid does not group: `data` is the page, so the grouping is held, ignored and
+warned about once. Group on the server and send the rows as they are to be shown.
+

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-grouping.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-grouping.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..89caaca
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-grid-grouping.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+import { useCallback, useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
+import { useWriteOnCommit } from '../../../internal/use-write-on-commit';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import { effectiveGrouping, sameGrouping } from '../engine/group';
+import type { DataGridExpandedGroups, DataGridGroupItem, DataGridPage } from '../types';
+import { sameList, useKept } from './use-kept';
+
+export interface GridGroupingOptions<TRow> {
+  /** The grouping as the grid holds it. */
+  grouping: readonly DataGridGroupItem[];
+  /** Every resolved column: a column the layout hides still groups. */
+  resolved: readonly ResolvedColumn<TRow>[];
+  /** Server mode groups nothing: the grouping is held, and the app groups on the server. */
+  remote: boolean;
+  /** `useGridState`'s setters and the reader of the open groups. */
+  setGrouping: (grouping: readonly DataGridGroupItem[]) => boolean;
+  setExpandedGroups: (expanded: DataGridExpandedGroups) => boolean;
+  expandedNow: () => DataGridExpandedGroups;
+  setPage: (page: DataGridPage) => void;
+  /** The page the state holds and its size, and whether the grid has pages. */
+  pageIndex: number;
+  size: number;
+  paged: boolean;
+  announce: (text: string) => void;
+}
+
+export interface GridGrouping {
+  /** The items that group, in order (`effectiveGrouping`); none in server mode. */
+  levels: readonly DataGridGroupItem[];
+  /** The fields of `levels`, kept by value: what the columns and the indents are made from. */
+  fields: readonly string[];
+  /**
+   * The one way the user changes the grouping (the panel and the menu call it): `onGroupingChange` and
+   * `onStateChange`, then the first page as a second change with its own pair of callbacks when the
+   * page was not the first, then `said`. A grouping that says what is held, or what an earlier request
+   * of the same event asked, does nothing at all.
+   */
+  applyGrouping: (next: readonly DataGridGroupItem[], said?: string) => void;
+  /** Opens or closes the group with this key: `onExpandedGroupsChange` and `onStateChange`, no sentence. */
+  toggleGroup: (key: string) => void;
+  expandAll: () => void;
+  collapseAll: () => void;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The grouping: which items group, and the three things the user does to it, each through one function
+ * so the callbacks, the page and what is said cannot differ between the parts that ask. The functions
+ * read what they need when they are called and are the same for as long as the grid lives, so a press
+ * on a group row draws no row but the ones it changes.
+ */
+export function useGridGrouping<TRow>(options: GridGroupingOptions<TRow>): GridGrouping {
+  const { grouping, resolved, remote } = options;
+  const levels = useKept(
+    useMemo(
+      () => (remote ? [] : effectiveGrouping(grouping, resolved)),
+      [grouping, resolved, remote],
+    ),
+    sameGrouping,
+  );
+  const fieldList = useMemo(() => levels.map((item) => item.field), [levels]);
+  const fields = useKept(fieldList, sameList);
+
+  const latest = useRef(options);
+  useWriteOnCommit(() => {
+    latest.current = options;
+  });
+
+  const applyGrouping = useCallback((next: readonly DataGridGroupItem[], said?: string) => {
+    const { setGrouping, setPage, pageIndex, size, paged, announce } = latest.current;
+    if (!setGrouping(next)) return;
+    if (paged && pageIndex !== 0) setPage({ index: 0, size });
+    if (said) announce(said);
+  }, []);
+
+  const toggleGroup = useCallback((key: string) => {
+    const { setExpandedGroups, expandedNow } = latest.current;
+    const now = expandedNow();
+    const except = now.except.includes(key)
+      ? now.except.filter((other) => other !== key)
+      : [...now.except, key];
+    setExpandedGroups({ allExpanded: now.allExpanded, except });
+  }, []);
+  const expandAll = useCallback(
+    () => void latest.current.setExpandedGroups({ allExpanded: true, except: [] }),
+    [],
+  );
+  const collapseAll = useCallback(
+    () => void latest.current.setExpandedGroups({ allExpanded: false, except: [] }),
+    [],
+  );
+  return { levels, fields, applyGrouping, toggleGroup, expandAll, collapseAll };
+}

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/parts/GroupRow.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/parts/GroupRow.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e1ba34a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/parts/GroupRow.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,161 @@
+import { memo } from 'react';
+import type { MouseEvent, ReactElement } from 'react';
+import { ChevronIcon } from '../../../internal/icons';
+import type { FlatGroupRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import type { PinPlace } from '../engine/layout';
+import { useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+import { highlightText } from '../highlight';
+import { useFoldedSearch } from '../search-context';
+import { IndentCell } from './IndentCells';
+import { pinAttributes } from './pin-attributes';
+
+interface GroupRowProps<TRow> {
+  flat: FlatGroupRow<TRow>;
+  /** Whether this row is the active place, the one Tab stop of the grid: a prop, so the keyboard draws only the rows it leaves and enters. */
+  active: boolean;
+  /** The place of the row for a screen reader, in a virtual grid, where the rows are not all drawn. */
+  ariaRowIndex: number | undefined;
+}
+
+// The pin of a cell that stands for a run of columns of one zone: the place of the first, and the edge
+// of the last, so the cell sticks where the run starts and ends the zone as the run does.
+function runPin(
+  pins: readonly (PinPlace | undefined)[],
+  from: number,
+  to: number,
+): PinPlace | undefined {
+  const first = pins[from];
+  return first ? { ...first, edge: pins[to]?.edge ?? false } : undefined;
+}
+
+function GroupRowImpl<TRow>({ flat, active, ariaRowIndex }: GroupRowProps<TRow>) {
+  const { layoutColumns, layoutPins, filler, labels, resolved, groups } = useGridContext<TRow>();
+  const search = useFoldedSearch();
+  const { node, level } = flat;
+  const column = resolved.find((candidate) => candidate.id === node.field);
+
+  // A press anywhere on the row toggles the group; the second click of a double press (`detail` 2 or
+  // more) is part of it and toggles nothing, so a double click opens the group once.
+  const onClick = (event: MouseEvent<HTMLTableRowElement>): void => {
+    if (event.detail > 1) return;
+    groups.toggle(flat.key);
+  };
+
+  // The cells in the order of the layout. Those before the chevron are empty (the band starts at the
+  // row's own chevron); the chevron stands in the indent column of the level; the caption goes on from
+  // there to the end of the left zone, or to the end of the row; the band goes on in an empty cell
+  // across the middle, and the cells of the right zone are empty, pinned.
+  const chevronAt =
+    layoutColumns.findIndex((candidate) => candidate.service === 'indent') + level - 1;
+  const cells: ReactElement[] = [];
+  layoutColumns.slice(0, chevronAt).forEach((candidate, at) => {
+    cells.push(<IndentCell key={candidate.id} pin={layoutPins[at]} />);
+  });
+  cells.push(
+    <td
+      key={layoutColumns[chevronAt]!.id}
+      className="flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-group-cell flg-data-grid-group-toggle"
+      {...pinAttributes(layoutPins[chevronAt])}
+    >
+      <span className="flg-data-grid-group-chevron" aria-hidden="true">
+        <ChevronIcon direction={flat.expanded ? 'down' : 'right'} width={16} height={16} />
+      </span>
+    </td>,
+  );
+  const rest = chevronAt + 1;
+  let leftEnd = rest;
+  while (leftEnd < layoutColumns.length && layoutPins[leftEnd]?.side === 'left') leftEnd++;
+  let rightStart = layoutColumns.length;
+  while (rightStart > leftEnd && layoutPins[rightStart - 1]?.side === 'right') rightStart--;
+  // The filler column sits before the right zone, or at the end: the middle takes it in.
+  const middle = rightStart - leftEnd + (filler ? 1 : 0);
+  const value =
+    node.value === null
+      ? labels.blank
+      : column?.allowSearch
+        ? highlightText(node.text, search)
+        : node.text;
+  const caption = (
+    <>
+      <span className="flg-data-grid-group-column">
+        {labels.groupColumn(column?.caption ?? node.field)}
+      </span>{' '}
+      <span className="flg-data-grid-group-value">{value}</span>{' '}
+      <span className="flg-data-grid-group-count">{labels.groupCount(node.rows.length)}</span>
+      {flat.continued ? (
+        <>
+          {' '}
+          <span className="flg-data-grid-group-continued">{labels.continued}</span>
+        </>
+      ) : null}
+    </>
+  );
+  const captionCell = (span: number, pin: PinPlace | undefined) => (
+    <td
+      key="flg:caption"
+      colSpan={span}
+      className="flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-group-cell flg-data-grid-group-caption"
+      {...pinAttributes(pin)}
+    >
+      {caption}
+    </td>
+  );
+  let captioned = true;
+  if (leftEnd > rest) {
+    cells.push(captionCell(leftEnd - rest, runPin(layoutPins, rest, leftEnd - 1)));
+    if (middle > 0) {
+      cells.push(
+        <td
+          key="flg:band"
+          colSpan={middle}
+          className="flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-group-cell"
+          aria-hidden="true"
+        />,
+      );
+    }
+  } else if (middle > 0) {
+    cells.push(captionCell(middle, undefined));
+  } else {
+    // Only the right zone is left of the row: its first cell carries the caption.
+    captioned = false;
+  }
+  for (let at = rightStart; at < layoutColumns.length; at++) {
+    if (!captioned) {
+      captioned = true;
+      cells.push(captionCell(1, layoutPins[at]));
+      continue;
+    }
+    cells.push(
+      <td
+        key={layoutColumns[at]!.id}
+        className="flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-group-cell"
+        aria-hidden="true"
+        {...pinAttributes(layoutPins[at])}
+      />,
+    );
+  }
+
+  return (
+    <tr
+      className="flg-table-row flg-data-grid-group-row"
+      data-level={level}
+      tabIndex={active ? 0 : -1}
+      aria-level={level}
+      aria-expanded={flat.expanded}
+      aria-setsize={flat.setsize}
+      aria-posinset={flat.posinset}
+      aria-rowindex={ariaRowIndex}
+      onClick={onClick}
+    >
+      {cells}
+    </tr>
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * The row of a group: a stop of the keyboard (`tabindex` on the row itself, never a control) with the
+ * chevron that says whether it is open, the group's column, value and count, and the band that runs
+ * across the rest of the row. A press on it toggles the group. Memoized: it draws again when its group
+ * row, whether it is the active place, or something the whole grid shares changes.
+ */
+export const GroupRow = memo(GroupRowImpl) as typeof GroupRowImpl;

  * The heading: the titles, and the filter row under them when the grid has one. Memoized: it takes

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
+import type { PinPlace } from '../engine/layout';
+import { useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+import { pinAttributes } from './pin-attributes';
+
+/**
+ * A cell of an indent column in a row of the body or in the filter row: the room a level of the
+ * grouping takes on the left. It holds nothing, is hidden from what reads the page, has no `tabindex`
+ * and is no place of the keyboard (`isPlaceColumn`, `cellsOf`). It is a cell of Table's classes, so its
+ * row's rule runs across it.
+ */
+export function IndentCell({ pin }: { pin: PinPlace | undefined }) {
+  return (
+    <td
+      className="flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-indent"
+      aria-hidden="true"
+      {...pinAttributes(pin)}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * The one cell of the heading that stands over the indent columns (`colSpan` their number), with the
+ * words `labels.groupsAndDetails` hidden in it: a table header with no name fails an accessibility
+ * check, so it is not `aria-hidden`. It is no place of the keyboard.
+ */
+export function IndentHead({ span, pin }: { span: number; pin: PinPlace | undefined }) {
+  const { labels } = useGridContext();
+  return (
+    <th
+      scope="col"
+      colSpan={span}
+      className="flg-table-head flg-data-grid-indent"
+      {...pinAttributes(pin)}
+    >
+      <span className="flg-visually-hidden">{labels.groupsAndDetails}</span>
+    </th>
+  );
+}
