+// ---- Moving rows (spec phase 6 §3.6, §3.8, §4.3 R1 "Kéo dòng", §6.3 "Kéo dòng") -------------------------
+
+/** The orders with the row `from` moved before or after the row `to`, as an app that does what it is told. */
+const movedRows = (
+  rows: readonly R1Order[],
+  from: DataGridKey,
+  to: DataGridKey,
+  position: DataGridRowDrop,
+): readonly R1Order[] => {
+  const moved = rows.find((one) => one.id === from)!;
+  const others = rows.filter((one) => one.id !== from);
+  const at = others.findIndex((one) => one.id === to) + (position === 'after' ? 1 : 0);
+  return [...others.slice(0, at), moved, ...others.slice(at)];
+};
+
+/** Four of R1's columns, for the grids that move rows: the keys and the drags need no more. */
+const MOVE_COLUMNS = R1_COLUMNS.filter((column) =>
+  ['id', 'customer', 'status', 'qty'].includes(String('field' in column ? column.field : '')),
+);
+
+/**
+ * A grid whose app does what `onRowReorder` says, as the app of the docs does: it moves the row in its own
+ * `data`. Unsorted and not grouped, since the handles do nothing while it is.
+ */
+const MovableGrid = ({
+  onMove,
+  ...props
+}: Partial<DataGridProps<R1Order>> & {
+  onMove?: (from: DataGridKey, to: DataGridKey, position: DataGridRowDrop) => void;
+}) => {
+  const [rows, setRows] = useState<readonly R1Order[]>(R1_ORDERS);
+  return (
+    <div style={{ width: 760, marginBottom: 24 }}>
+      <DataGrid
+        aria-label="Orders"
+        data={rows}
+        rowKey="id"
+        columns={MOVE_COLUMNS}
+        paging={false}
+        rowReorder
+        onRowReorder={(from, to, position) => {
+          onMove?.(from, to, position);
+          setRows((now) => movedRows(now, from, to, position));
+        }}
+        {...props}
+      />
+    </div>
+  );
+};
+
+/** The data rows of the grid's own body, in order. */
+const dataRowsOf = (root: HTMLElement) =>
+  bodyRowsOf(root).filter((row) => row.classList.contains('flg-data-grid-row'));
+/** The keys of the data rows, in order: the text of the row header. */
+const orderOf = (root: HTMLElement) =>
+  dataRowsOf(root).map((row) => row.querySelector('th')?.textContent);
+const handleOf = (root: HTMLElement, key: string) =>
+  root.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(`button[aria-label="Reorder ${key}"]`)!;
+/** The line a drag of a row draws, `null` when it draws none. */
+const rowLineOf = (root: HTMLElement) =>
+  root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-drop-line[data-axis="y"]');
+
+/** The ids of R1's orders, in the order the stories start from. */
+const START_ORDER = R1_ORDERS.map((one) => one.id);
+
+/**
+ * How long a story waits for the menu of a row, which fades in from `opacity: 0` and which Linux WebKit on
+ * x86 (CI) takes up to ten seconds over (`KeysInPopup` of `DataGrid.stories.tsx`).
+ */
+const MENU_SHOWN = { timeout: 10000 };
+
+/**
+ * `mod+Shift+↑` and `mod+Shift+↓` on a cell of a row, with real keys (spec phase 6 §3.6): Tab lands on the
+ * first handle (the active place of a grid is its first cell), the arrows go down to the third row, and
+ * the key moves it up one place and then to the top, where it does nothing more; two presses down move it
+ * two places; on a cell of data the same key moves the row, and the cell keeps the focus. After each move
+ * the focus is on the same row at the same column, wherever the row went, and the grid has its one Tab
+ * stop. The story asserts what each burst of keys ends in, never how many calls it made.
+ */
+function rowReorderKeys(mod: 'Control' | 'Meta'): NonNullable<Story['play']> {
+  return async ({ canvasElement, args }) => {
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    const table = tableOf(root);
+    const calls = args.onRowReorder as ReturnType<typeof fn>;
+    const press = (key: string) => real.keyboard(`{${mod}>}{Shift>}{${key}}{/Shift}{/${mod}}`);
+    const active = () => document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
+    const inRow = (key: string, column: number) =>
+      dataRowsOf(root).find((row) => row.querySelector('th')?.textContent === key)!.cells[column]!;
+    await expect(orderOf(root)).toEqual(START_ORDER);
+    for (let tabs = 0; tabs < 4 && !table.contains(document.activeElement); tabs += 1) {
+      await real.tab();
+    }
+    await expect(active()).toBe(handleOf(root, 'DH-1034'));
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowDown}{ArrowDown}');
+    await expect(active()).toBe(handleOf(root, 'DH-1030'));
+
+    await press('ArrowUp');
+    await waitFor(
+      () =>
+        expect(orderOf(root).slice(0, 3), 'DH-1030 is the second').toEqual([
+          'DH-1034',
+          'DH-1030',
+          'DH-1031',
+        ]),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(active(), 'the focus stays on its handle').toBe(handleOf(root, 'DH-1030')),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(calls).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('DH-1030', 'DH-1031', 'before');
+    await press('ArrowUp');
+    await waitFor(
+      () =>
+        expect(orderOf(root).slice(0, 2), 'DH-1030 is the first').toEqual(['DH-1030', 'DH-1034']),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    // At the top the key moves nothing and asks for nothing.
+    const atTop = calls.mock.calls.length;
+    await press('ArrowUp');
+    await nextFrame();
+    await expect(orderOf(root).slice(0, 2)).toEqual(['DH-1030', 'DH-1034']);
+    await expect(calls.mock.calls.length, 'nothing was asked at the edge').toBe(atTop);
+    await expect(active()).toBe(handleOf(root, 'DH-1030'));
+
+    // Two presses down end two places lower.
+    await press('ArrowDown');
+    await press('ArrowDown');
+    await waitFor(
+      () =>
+        expect(orderOf(root).slice(0, 3), 'DH-1030 is the third').toEqual([
+          'DH-1034',
+          'DH-1031',
+          'DH-1030',
+        ]),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+
+    // On a cell of data: the Customer cell of the row moves it, and keeps the focus.
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowRight}{ArrowRight}');
+    await expect(active()).toBe(inRow('DH-1030', 2));
+    await press('ArrowUp');
+    await waitFor(
+      () =>
+        expect(orderOf(root).slice(0, 3), 'DH-1030 is the second again').toEqual([
+          'DH-1034',
+          'DH-1030',
+          'DH-1031',
+        ]),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(active(), 'the focus is on its Customer cell').toBe(inRow('DH-1030', 2)),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(table.querySelectorAll('[tabindex="0"]'), 'one Tab stop').toHaveLength(1);
+    await expect(table.contains(active())).toBe(true);
+  };
+}
+
+export const RowReorderKeys: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  beforeEach: onPlatform('other'),
+  args: { onRowReorder: fn() },
+  render: (args) => <MovableGrid onMove={args.onRowReorder} />,
+  play: rowReorderKeys('Control'),
+};
+
+export const RowReorderKeysOnAMac: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  beforeEach: onPlatform('apple'),
+  args: { onRowReorder: fn() },
+  render: (args) => <MovableGrid onMove={args.onRowReorder} />,
+  play: rowReorderKeys('Meta'),
+};
+
+/**
+ * The menu of a row, with real keys (spec phase 6 §3.6): Enter on a handle opens it, on its first item;
+ * the arrows go down it, and Enter on "Move to bottom" moves the row and closes the menu, and the focus is
+ * on the handle of the row, which is now the last; "Move down" and "Move to bottom" are off for it. Space
+ * opens it too, and Escape closes it and gives the focus back to the handle.
+ */
+export const RowMenuKeys: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  beforeEach: onPlatform('other'),
+  args: { onRowReorder: fn() },
+  render: (args) => <MovableGrid onMove={args.onRowReorder} />,
+  play: async ({ canvasElement, args }) => {
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    const table = tableOf(root);
+    const calls = args.onRowReorder as ReturnType<typeof fn>;
+    const active = () => document.activeElement as HTMLElement;
+    const menu = () => document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-row-menu')!;
+    const opened = () => menu().matches(':popover-open');
+    const items = () => Array.from(menu().querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[role="menuitem"]'));
+    for (let tabs = 0; tabs < 4 && !table.contains(document.activeElement); tabs += 1) {
+      await real.tab();
+    }
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowDown}{ArrowDown}');
+    await expect(active()).toBe(handleOf(root, 'DH-1030'));
+
+    await real.keyboard('{Enter}');
+    await waitFor(() => expect(opened(), 'the menu is open').toBe(true), MENU_SHOWN);
+    await expect(handleOf(root, 'DH-1030')).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
+    await expect(items().map((item) => item.textContent)).toEqual([
+      'Move up',
+      'Move down',
+      'Move to top',
+      'Move to bottom',
+    ]);
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(active().textContent, 'the first item has the focus').toBe('Move up'),
+      MENU_SHOWN,
+    );
+    await real.keyboard('{ArrowDown}{ArrowDown}{ArrowDown}');
+    await expect(active().textContent).toBe('Move to bottom');
+    await real.keyboard('{Enter}');
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(orderOf(root).at(-1), 'DH-1030 is the last row').toBe('DH-1030'),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(calls).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('DH-1030', 'DH-1037', 'after');
+    await waitFor(() => expect(opened(), 'the menu is closed').toBe(false), MENU_SHOWN);
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(active(), 'the focus is on its handle').toBe(handleOf(root, 'DH-1030')),
+      MENU_SHOWN,
+    );
+
+    // The last row cannot go down: its two items are off. Space opens the menu, Escape closes it.
+    await real.keyboard(' ');
+    await waitFor(() => expect(opened(), 'Space opens the menu').toBe(true), MENU_SHOWN);
+    const off = items()
+      .filter((item) => item.getAttribute('aria-disabled') === 'true')
+      .map((item) => item.textContent);
+    await expect(off).toEqual(['Move down', 'Move to bottom']);
+    await real.keyboard('{Escape}');
+    await waitFor(() => expect(opened(), 'Escape closes the menu').toBe(false), MENU_SHOWN);
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(active(), 'the focus is on its handle').toBe(handleOf(root, 'DH-1030')),
+      MENU_SHOWN,
+    );
+    await expect(orderOf(root).at(-1)).toBe('DH-1030');
+  },
+};
+
+/** The grid and the page have none of what a drag sets on them. */
+async function dragIsOver(root: HTMLElement, what: string) {
+  await nextFrame();
+  await expect(document.documentElement, `${what}: the cursor mark is gone`).not.toHaveAttribute(
+    'data-flg-grid-cursor',
+  );
+  await expect(
+    document.querySelector('.flg-data-grid-drag-chip'),
+    `${what}: the chip is gone`,
+  ).toBeNull();
+  await expect(rowLineOf(root), `${what}: the line is gone`).toBeNull();
+  await expect(root.querySelector('[data-drag-source]'), `${what}: no row is dimmed`).toBeNull();
+}
+
+/**
+ * Moving a row by the mouse, in each engine (spec phase 6 §3.8, §4.3 R1 "Kéo dòng"). The states that need
+ * the button held are made with pointer events the browser does not know: the row at 35%, the chip with its
+ * name 16px from the pointer, the line 3px across what the frame shows with its dot, at the boundary a drop
+ * would use and nowhere beside the row itself, the cursor mark, and a frame that scrolls under a pointer
+ * at its edge. Escape puts everything back. The drops are made with the real mouse: after the lower half of
+ * a row, and before the upper half of another.
+ */
+export const RowReorderMouse: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  args: { onRowReorder: fn() },
+  render: (args) => <MovableGrid onMove={args.onRowReorder} height={300} />,
+  play: async ({ canvasElement, args }) => {
+    const real = await realUserEvent();
+    if (!real) return;
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    const frame = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-frame')!;
+    const calls = args.onRowReorder as ReturnType<typeof fn>;
+    await expect(orderOf(root)).toEqual(START_ORDER);
+
+    // A held drag of the first row, to the lower half of the third.
+    const handle = handleOf(root, 'DH-1034');
+    const start = middleOf(handle);
+    const send = pointer('mouse', 91, start);
+    const third = dataRowsOf(root)[2]!.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const target = { x: start.x + 100, y: third.top + third.height * 0.75 };
+    send(handle, 'pointerdown');
+    send(document, 'pointermove', target);
+    await waitFor(() => expect(rowLineOf(root), 'the line is drawn').not.toBeNull(), RENDER_UPDATE);
+    const line = rowLineOf(root)!;
+    const box = line.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const inner = frame.getBoundingClientRect();
+    near(box.height, 3, 0.5, 'the line is 3px high');
+    near(box.top + box.height / 2, third.bottom, 1.5, 'its middle is on the boundary under row 3');
+    near(
+      box.left,
+      inner.left + frame.clientLeft,
+      1,
+      'it starts at the left of what the frame shows',
+    );
+    near(box.width, frame.clientWidth, 1.5, 'and runs across what it shows');
+    const dot = getComputedStyle(line, '::before');
+    await expect([dot.width, dot.height, dot.left]).toEqual(['7px', '7px', '-2px']);
+    await expect(dot.backgroundColor, 'the dot and the line are the accent').toBe(
+      getComputedStyle(line).backgroundColor,
+    );
+    await expect(getComputedStyle(line).pointerEvents).toBe('none');
+    const chip = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid-drag-chip')!;
+    await expect(chip).toHaveTextContent('DH-1034');
+    near(
+      chip.getBoundingClientRect().left,
+      target.x + 16,
+      1.5,
+      'the chip is 16px right of the pointer',
+    );
+    near(chip.getBoundingClientRect().top, target.y + 16, 1.5, 'and 16px below it');
+    await expect(getComputedStyle(dataRowsOf(root)[0]!).opacity, 'the source row is at 35%').toBe(
+      '0.35',
+    );
+    await expect(dataRowsOf(root)[1]!).not.toHaveAttribute('data-drag-source');
+    await expect(document.documentElement).toHaveAttribute('data-flg-grid-cursor', 'grabbing');
+    // Over the row itself there is no line: a drop there would move nothing.
+    send(document, 'pointermove', middleOf(dataRowsOf(root)[0]!));
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(rowLineOf(root), 'no line over the row itself').toBeNull(),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    // Over the heading there is none either.
+    send(document, 'pointermove', middleOf(titleOf(root, 'Customer')));
+    await nextFrame();
+    await expect(rowLineOf(root), 'no line over the heading').toBeNull();
+    // Escape puts everything back, and the release after it moves nothing.
+    send(document, 'pointermove', target);
+    await waitFor(() => expect(rowLineOf(root)).not.toBeNull(), RENDER_UPDATE);
+    await real.keyboard('{Escape}');
+    await dragIsOver(root, 'Escape');
+    send(document, 'pointerup', target);
+    await nextFrame();
+    await expect(calls).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    await expect(orderOf(root)).toEqual(START_ORDER);
+
+    // The frame scrolls under a pointer at its bottom edge, and the cancel ends it.
+    send(handle, 'pointerdown');
+    send(document, 'pointermove', { x: start.x + 100, y: inner.bottom - 6 });
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(frame.scrollTop, 'the frame scrolled').toBeGreaterThan(0),
+      SCROLL_EVENT,
+    );
+    send(document, 'pointermove', target);
+    send(document, 'pointercancel');
+    await dragIsOver(root, 'a cancel');
+    await expect(calls).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
+    frame.scrollTop = 0;
+    await waitFor(() => expect(frame.scrollTop).toBe(0), SCROLL_EVENT);
+
+    // The real mouse: the first row dropped on the lower half of the fourth.
+    const rows = () => dataRowsOf(root);
+    const fourth = rows()[3]!.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const grip = handle.getBoundingClientRect();
+    await real.dragAndDrop(handle, rows()[3]!, {
+      sourcePosition: { x: grip.width / 2, y: grip.height / 2 },
+      targetPosition: { x: 100, y: fourth.height * 0.75 },
+    });
+    await waitFor(
+      () =>
+        expect(orderOf(root).slice(0, 4), 'DH-1034 is after DH-1027').toEqual([
+          'DH-1031',
+          'DH-1030',
+          'DH-1027',
+          'DH-1034',
+        ]),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(calls).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('DH-1034', 'DH-1027', 'after');
+    await dragIsOver(root, 'the first drop');
+
+    // And the fifth row before the upper half of the first.
+    const first = rows()[0]!.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const fifth = handleOf(root, 'DH-1022').getBoundingClientRect();
+    await real.dragAndDrop(handleOf(root, 'DH-1022'), rows()[0]!, {
+      sourcePosition: { x: fifth.width / 2, y: fifth.height / 2 },
+      targetPosition: { x: 100, y: first.height * 0.25 },
+    });
+    await waitFor(
+      () => expect(orderOf(root)[0], 'DH-1022 is the first').toBe('DH-1022'),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(calls).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('DH-1022', 'DH-1031', 'before');
+    await dragIsOver(root, 'the second drop');
+  },
+};
+
+/**
+ * A finger moves a row (spec phase 6 §3.8, Claude's ruling on the touch drags). The story runner cannot make a
+ * touch drag (Playwright's touchscreen only taps), so the finger is a pointer of type `touch` that the page
+ * dispatches, which the grid follows as it follows the real one; the unit tests of the grid do the same with
+ * a touch pointer. The handle takes every pointer type and has `touch-action: none`, so the browser's own
+ * scroll does not take the finger.
+ */
+export const RowReorderTouch: Story = {
+  tags: ['no-visual'],
+  args: { onRowReorder: fn() },
+  render: (args) => <MovableGrid onMove={args.onRowReorder} />,
+  play: async ({ canvasElement, args }) => {
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    const calls = args.onRowReorder as ReturnType<typeof fn>;
+    const handle = handleOf(root, 'DH-1031');
+    await expect(getComputedStyle(handle).touchAction).toBe('none');
+    const finger = pointer('touch', 95, middleOf(handle));
+    const fourth = dataRowsOf(root)[3]!.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const to = { x: middleOf(handle).x + 60, y: fourth.top + fourth.height * 0.25 };
+    finger(handle, 'pointerdown');
+    finger(document, 'pointermove', to);
+    await waitFor(() => expect(rowLineOf(root), 'the line is drawn').not.toBeNull(), RENDER_UPDATE);
+    await expect(dataRowsOf(root)[1]!).toHaveAttribute('data-drag-source');
+    finger(document, 'pointerup', to);
+    await waitFor(
+      () =>
+        expect(orderOf(root).slice(0, 4), 'DH-1031 is before DH-1027').toEqual([
+          'DH-1034',
+          'DH-1030',
+          'DH-1031',
+          'DH-1027',
+        ]),
+      RENDER_UPDATE,
+    );
+    await expect(calls).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('DH-1031', 'DH-1027', 'before');
+    await dragIsOver(root, 'the finger');
+  },
+};
+
+/**
+ * Outside the mockup (spec phase 6 §4.3 R1 "Kéo dòng", after D2 and C1): G1's grid with the column of
+ * handles after the boxes, unsorted, and the handle of the third row held down and dragged to between the
+ * fifth and the sixth rows (the harness drags what has `data-visual-drag` by the distance it says, and
+ * shoots with the button down): the handle column, the third row at 35% with its handle in the accent, the
+ * chip with its name 16px from the pointer, and the 3px line across the frame with its dot at its left end,
+ * on the boundary under the fifth row. The pointer ends in the lower half of the fifth row, so the stage
+ * holds the chip.
+ */
+export const RowReorderDragging: Story = {
+  tags: ['viewport-1440x720'],
+  render: () => (
+    <SalesGrid variant="lined" height={459} defaultSort={[]} rowReorder onRowReorder={() => {}} />
+  ),
+  play: async ({ canvasElement }) => {
+    const root = canvasElement.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.flg-data-grid')!;
+    const rows = Array.from(
+      root.querySelectorAll<HTMLTableRowElement>('tbody > tr.flg-data-grid-row'),
+    );
+    await expect(rows).toHaveLength(12);
+    // The column of handles is 28px, after the boxes and before the data.
+    const head = root.querySelector<HTMLElement>('th[data-service="drag"]')!;
+    await expect(Math.round(head.offsetWidth)).toBe(28);
+    await expect(
+      Array.from(rows[0]!.cells)
+        .slice(0, 3)
+        .map((cell) => cell.getAttribute('data-service')),
+    ).toEqual(['select', 'drag', null]);
+    const handle = rows[2]!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('button.flg-data-grid-row-handle')!;
+    await expect(handle).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', 'Reorder DH-1033');
+    for (const row of rows) {
+      await expect(
+        row.querySelector('button.flg-data-grid-row-handle'),
+        'every row has its handle, none of them off',
+      ).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-disabled');
+    }
+    const box = handle.getBoundingClientRect();
+    await expect([Math.round(box.width), Math.round(box.height)], 'the handle is 20 by 24').toEqual(
+      [20, 24],
+    );
+    // The pointer ends in the lower half of the fifth row: the boundary under it is where the line stands.
+    const fifth = rows[4]!.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const end = fifth.bottom - fifth.height / 4;
+    const dy = Math.round(end - (box.top + box.height / 2));
+    handle.setAttribute('data-visual-drag', `0,${dy}`);
+    // The chip is 16px below the pointer and about 28px tall: the stage has the room.
+    const stage = canvasElement.closest<HTMLElement>('[data-testid="flg-stage"]');
+    if (stage) {
+      await expect(stage.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - end).toBeGreaterThan(16 + 28);
+    }
+    await noTitleIsCut(root);
+  },
+};

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/engine/row-reorder.test.ts b/src/components/data-grid/engine/row-reorder.test.ts

index 0000000..3a1b397
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/engine/row-reorder.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
+import { askOfMove, isPlacedAs, pagePlaces, placeAfterMove, rowDrop } from './row-reorder';
+import type { RowBlock } from './row-reorder';
+
+// What a move of a row asks (spec phase 6 §6.3 "Kéo dòng"), where it puts the row, and where a drop at a point
+// goes (§3.8): the pure rules, which the keys, the menu and the drag all use.
+
+const KEYS = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'];
+
+describe('askOfMove', () => {
+  it('asks up before the row above, down after the row below', () => {
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'c', 'up')).toEqual({ toKey: 'b', position: 'before' });
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'b', 'down')).toEqual({ toKey: 'c', position: 'after' });
+  });
+
+  it('asks top before the first row and bottom after the last', () => {
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'c', 'top')).toEqual({ toKey: 'a', position: 'before' });
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'b', 'bottom')).toEqual({ toKey: 'd', position: 'after' });
+    // The second row goes before the first, which is a move: the menu's top is not "already there".
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'b', 'top')).toEqual({ toKey: 'a', position: 'before' });
+  });
+
+  it('asks nothing at an edge, where the row cannot go that way', () => {
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'a', 'up')).toBeNull();
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'a', 'top')).toBeNull();
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'd', 'down')).toBeNull();
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'd', 'bottom')).toBeNull();
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'a', 'down')).not.toBeNull();
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'd', 'up')).not.toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  it('asks nothing for a row that is not among the keys, or for the only row', () => {
+    expect(askOfMove(KEYS, 'x', 'up')).toBeNull();
+    expect(askOfMove(['a'], 'a', 'down')).toBeNull();
+    expect(askOfMove([], 'a', 'up')).toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  it('compares numbers and strings as they are', () => {
+    expect(askOfMove([1, '1', 2], '1', 'up')).toEqual({ toKey: 1, position: 'before' });
+    expect(askOfMove([1, 2], '2', 'up')).toBeNull();
+  });
+});
+
+describe('placeAfterMove', () => {
+  it('counts from 1 the place the row has once it has moved', () => {
+    expect(placeAfterMove(KEYS, 'c', { toKey: 'b', position: 'before' })).toBe(2);
+    expect(placeAfterMove(KEYS, 'b', { toKey: 'c', position: 'after' })).toBe(3);
+    expect(placeAfterMove(KEYS, 'c', { toKey: 'a', position: 'before' })).toBe(1);
+    expect(placeAfterMove(KEYS, 'a', { toKey: 'd', position: 'after' })).toBe(4);
+    expect(placeAfterMove(KEYS, 'a', { toKey: 'c', position: 'before' })).toBe(2);
+  });
+
+  it('is 0 where nothing moves: itself, a row that is not there, a row that is not asked for', () => {
+    expect(placeAfterMove(KEYS, 'b', { toKey: 'b', position: 'after' })).toBe(0);
+    expect(placeAfterMove(KEYS, 'x', { toKey: 'b', position: 'after' })).toBe(0);
+    expect(placeAfterMove(KEYS, 'b', { toKey: 'x', position: 'after' })).toBe(0);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('isPlacedAs', () => {
+  it('holds when the row is right before or right after the row it was moved to', () => {
+    expect(isPlacedAs(['a', 'c', 'b', 'd'], 'c', { toKey: 'b', position: 'before' })).toBe(true);
+    expect(isPlacedAs(['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'], 'c', { toKey: 'b', position: 'after' })).toBe(true);
+  });
+
+  it('does not hold for rows in another order, or a row that is gone', () => {
+    expect(isPlacedAs(KEYS, 'c', { toKey: 'b', position: 'before' })).toBe(false);
+    expect(isPlacedAs(['b', 'a', 'c', 'd'], 'c', { toKey: 'b', position: 'before' })).toBe(false);
+    expect(isPlacedAs(['a', 'b'], 'c', { toKey: 'b', position: 'after' })).toBe(false);
+    expect(isPlacedAs(KEYS, 'c', { toKey: 'x', position: 'after' })).toBe(false);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('pagePlaces', () => {
+  it('numbers the data rows of the page and skips the others', () => {
+    const places = pagePlaces([
+      { kind: 'data', key: 'a' },
+      { kind: 'detail', key: 'a' },
+      { kind: 'data', key: 'b' },
+      { kind: 'group', key: 'g' },
+      { kind: 'data', key: 'c' },
+    ]);
+    expect([...places]).toEqual([
+      ['a', 0],
+      ['b', 1],
+      ['c', 2],
+    ]);
+  });
+
+  it('keeps the first place of a key that two rows have', () => {
+    const places = pagePlaces([
+      { kind: 'data', key: 'a' },
+      { kind: 'data', key: 'a' },
+      { kind: 'data', key: 'b' },
+    ]);
+    expect([...places]).toEqual([
+      ['a', 0],
+      ['b', 1],
+    ]);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('rowDrop', () => {
+  // Four rows of 30px from y 100, the second with a detail of 60px under it.
+  const blocks: RowBlock[] = [
+    { key: 'a', place: 0, top: 100, middle: 115, bottom: 130 },
+    { key: 'b', place: 1, top: 130, middle: 145, bottom: 220 },
+    { key: 'c', place: 2, top: 220, middle: 235, bottom: 250 },
+    { key: 'd', place: 3, top: 250, middle: 265, bottom: 280 },
+  ];
+
+  it('drops before the row in its upper half, after it in its lower half, the line on the boundary', () => {
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 0, 255)).toEqual({
+      ask: { toKey: 'd', position: 'before' },
+      y: 250,
+    });
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 0, 275)).toEqual({ ask: { toKey: 'd', position: 'after' }, y: 280 });
+  });
+
+  it('puts the line of a drop after a row that has its detail open under the detail', () => {
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 3, 160)).toEqual({ ask: { toKey: 'b', position: 'after' }, y: 220 });
+  });
+
+  it('moves nothing beside the row: before and after itself, and next to it', () => {
+    // The row `c` (place 2): before itself, after itself, after `b` and before `d` are its own place.
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 2, 225)).toBeNull();
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 2, 245)).toBeNull();
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 2, 200)).toBeNull();
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 2, 255)).toBeNull();
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 2, 135)).not.toBeNull();
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 2, 275)).not.toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  it('works from the place of a row that is not drawn (a virtual window scrolled past it)', () => {
+    // The source is the row at place 10, above every block: every drop is before it or beyond.
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 10, 105)).toEqual({ ask: { toKey: 'a', position: 'before' }, y: 100 });
+  });
+
+  it('is nothing outside the rows', () => {
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 0, 99)).toBeNull();
+    expect(rowDrop(blocks, 0, 280)).toBeNull();
+    expect(rowDrop([], 0, 120)).toBeNull();
+  });
+});

+const boxOf = (left: number, top: number, right: number, bottom: number) =>
+  ({
+    left,
+    top,
+    right,
+    bottom,
+    x: left,
+    y: top,
+    width: right - left,
+    height: bottom - top,
+    toJSON: () => ({}),

+describe('placeLine', () => {
+  afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks());
+
+  /** A line in a main box at (20, 10), 400 by 300 and drawn at its own size, over a frame inside it. */
+  function lineIn(scale = 1) {
+    const main = document.createElement('div');
+    const frame = document.createElement('div');
+    const line = document.createElement('div');
+    main.append(frame, line);
+    document.body.append(main);
+    vi.spyOn(main, 'getBoundingClientRect').mockReturnValue(boxOf(20, 10, 20 + 400 * scale, 310));
+    vi.spyOn(main, 'offsetWidth', 'get').mockReturnValue(400);
+    // The frame starts 2px inside the main box, with a 1px border, and shows 380 by 200.
+    vi.spyOn(frame, 'getBoundingClientRect').mockReturnValue(boxOf(22, 12, 405, 215));
+    vi.spyOn(frame, 'clientLeft', 'get').mockReturnValue(1);
+    vi.spyOn(frame, 'clientTop', 'get').mockReturnValue(1);
+    vi.spyOn(frame, 'clientWidth', 'get').mockReturnValue(380);
+    vi.spyOn(frame, 'clientHeight', 'get').mockReturnValue(200);
+    return { line, frame, main };
+  }
+
+  it('places a vertical line from its start to the bottom of what the frame shows, centred on x', () => {
+    const { line, frame, main } = lineIn();
+    const inside = placeLine(line, frame, 100, 40, 3);
+    expect(line.style.left).toBe('78.5px');
+    expect(line.style.top).toBe('30px');
+    // The frame shows down to 12 + 1 + 200 = 213: the line is 213 - 40 = 173px tall.
+    expect(line.style.height).toBe('173px');
+    expect(inside).toBe(true);
+    // x outside what the frame shows sideways (23..403) says so.
+    expect(placeLine(line, frame, 10, 40, 3)).toBe(false);
+    expect(placeLine(line, frame, 404, 40, 3, 'x')).toBe(false);
+    main.remove();
+  });
+
+  it('places a horizontal line from its start to the right edge of what the frame shows, centred on y', () => {
+    const { line, frame, main } = lineIn();
+    const inside = placeLine(line, frame, 100, 23, 3, 'y');
+    expect(line.style.left).toBe('3px');
+    expect(line.style.top).toBe('88.5px');
+    // The frame shows 23..403 sideways: from 23 the line is 380px wide.
+    expect(line.style.width).toBe('380px');
+    expect(inside).toBe(true);
+    // y outside what the frame shows vertically (13..213) says so.
+    expect(placeLine(line, frame, 12, 23, 3, 'y')).toBe(false);
+    expect(placeLine(line, frame, 214, 23, 3, 'y')).toBe(false);
+    main.remove();
+  });
+
+  it('writes layout pixels, scaled back by the one the grid is drawn at', () => {
+    const { line, frame, main } = lineIn(0.5);
+    placeLine(line, frame, 120, 23, 3, 'y');
+    // Drawn at half its size: the main box is 200px wide on the screen, and 400 in layout.
+    expect(line.style.top).toBe(`${(120 - 10) * 2 - 1.5}px`);
+    expect(line.style.left).toBe(`${(23 - 20) * 2}px`);
+    expect(line.style.width).toBe(`${(403 - 23) * 2}px`);
+    main.remove();
+  });
+
+  it('places nothing and says no for a line that is in no box', () => {

+    expect(line.style.left).toBe('');

+});

+describe('rowBlocks', () => {
+  afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks());
+
+  function bodyOf(kinds: ('data' | 'detail' | 'group' | 'spacer')[], virtualFrom?: number) {
+    const table = document.createElement('table');
+    const body = table.createTBody();
+    const boxes = new Map<HTMLTableRowElement, DOMRect>();
+    let top = 50;
+    kinds.forEach((kind, at) => {
+      const row = body.insertRow();
+      row.className =
+        kind === 'data'
+          ? 'flg-data-grid-row'
+          : kind === 'detail'
+            ? 'flg-data-grid-detail-row'
+            : kind === 'group'
+              ? 'flg-data-grid-group-row'
+              : 'flg-data-grid-spacer';
+      if (virtualFrom !== undefined && kind !== 'spacer') {
+        row.setAttribute('aria-rowindex', String(virtualFrom + at));
+      }
+      const height = kind === 'detail' ? 80 : 30;
+      boxes.set(row, boxOf(0, top, 100, top + height));
+      top += height;
+    });
+    vi.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'getBoundingClientRect').mockImplementation(function (
+      this: HTMLElement,
+    ) {
+      return boxes.get(this as HTMLTableRowElement) ?? boxOf(0, 0, 0, 0);
+    });
+    return table;
+  }
+

+      { key: 'k0', top: 50, middle: 65, bottom: 80 },
+      { key: 'k1', top: 80, middle: 95, bottom: 190 },
+      { key: 'k3', top: 190, middle: 205, bottom: 220 },

+  });
+
+  it('leaves out the rows that have no key, the group rows and the spacers', () => {

+      { key: 'x', top: 140, middle: 155, bottom: 170 },
+    ]);
+  });
+

+    const asked: number[] = [];
+    rowBlocks(table, (index) => {
+      asked.push(index);
+      return index;
+    });
+    expect(asked).toEqual([40, 41]);
+  });
+});

(2) Menu và phím đếm trên mọi trang, kéo thả đếm trong trang đang xem (chỉ các dòng đang vẽ là đích). (3) Tay nắm khi tắt vẫn nhận focus để người dùng bàn phím đọc được lý do; Tooltip của nó là mô tả của nút (`describe` mặc định, vì chữ của Tooltip không phải tên nút). (4) Menu đóng khi `rowReorder` tắt, khi grid bắt đầu sắp xếp hay nhóm và khi dòng của nó rời các dòng đang thấy; focus về nhà của ô hoạt động, tức tay nắm của dòng (vị trí theo khoá). (5) Một lần chuyển bằng menu hay phím được theo: ở commit đầu tiên có `data` khác với `data` lúc hỏi, nếu các dòng đúng thứ tự đã hỏi (dòng nằm ngay trước hay sau `toKey`), grid gọi `scrollToRow` (sang trang của dòng nếu nó ở trang khác, một lần, rồi cuộn dòng vào tầm nhìn ít nhất có thể); dòng rời trang đã để vị trí hoạt động lại cho dòng bên cạnh, nên commit hiện dòng ở trang của nó trả vị trí và focus (nếu grid đang giữ focus) cho dòng. Commit đầu tiên đó kết thúc yêu cầu dù thấy gì (không đồng hồ): `data` do app đổi theo cách khác không bị kéo trang, và một lần chuyển mà app không bao giờ trả lời thì không chờ gì ngoài một lần `data` đổi. Một lần thả không được theo (con trỏ đang ở trên dòng). (6) Kéo: một `usePointerDrag` cho mọi tay nắm, mọi loại con trỏ; `mousedown` bị huỷ chứ không phải `pointerdown`, tay nắm tự lấy focus; dòng gốc, chip, vạch, dấu con trỏ, tự cuộn và nghe `scroll` đều được gỡ ở mọi đường kết thúc (thả, Esc, `pointercancel`, mất capture, grid gỡ, `rowReorder` tắt hay grid bắt đầu sắp xếp hay nhóm); chỉ thả mới gọi `onRowReorder`, theo nơi vạch đứng tính lại từ DOM lúc thả; vị trí của dòng gốc tính theo danh sách chứ không theo DOM, nên cuộn ảo kéo qua nó vẫn thả được. Tự cuộn theo trục `y` chỉ khi grid có `height`. `placeLine` đặt cả vạch ngang (`axis: 'y'`), `DragView` mang `axis` và khoá dòng.

 Rows of data in typed columns, drawn in the look of a [Table](?path=/docs/components-table--docs).
 The grid is the part of the library that knows about the data. It is built in steps: today it reads
 the columns, formats each value for its type and its locale, draws the rows with a sticky heading,
-sorts them, pages them, chooses rows, draws a long list by windows, filters them (a search field
+sorts them, pages them, chooses rows, groups them with totals, opens a detail under a row, moves rows, draws a long list by windows, filters them (a search field
 that marks what it finds, a row of filter cells, a funnel on each title that lists the values, and a
 bar that says the conditions), says when it loads and when it is empty, and has a keyboard.
 
@@ -447,7 +447,7 @@ nothing.
 
 A column that can be resized has a handle on the right edge of its title: a thin line between the
 titles that becomes a bar of 3px in the accent under the pointer. `allowResizing` is the default of
-every column (`true`), and a column's own `allowResizing` wins; the column of boxes has no handle.
+every column (`true`), and a column's own `allowResizing` wins; the column of boxes and the column of row handles have none.
 The handle is for a pointer: it is hidden from a screen reader and is no stop of Tab, so the keys
 below are the way for everyone else.
 
@@ -511,12 +511,14 @@ colour and the bar is `Highlight`; with more contrast the line is solid.
 | Move a column        | Drag the title                                      | No: a finger on a title scrolls the frame                                    | <Kbd keys="mod+shift+left" /> <Kbd keys="mod+shift+right" /> |

 ## Reordering columns

+## Reordering rows
+
+`rowReorder` gives the grid a column of handles, 28px wide, after the column of boxes and before the
+indent columns of a grouping, and lets a person move a row: by a drag of its handle, by a menu that
+the handle opens, and by keys. **The grid moves nothing.** It tells `onRowReorder(fromKey, toKey,
+position)` and your app changes `data`: the row `fromKey` goes `'before'` or `'after'` the row
+`toKey`. Both rows are among the rows after the filter, in the order they are shown, so a move in a
+filtered grid is counted among the rows the filter keeps, and one in a grid with pages is counted
+over every page (in server mode, over the rows of the page: see below). `rowReorder` is for `true`
+and no other value. Without `onRowReorder` the handles are drawn, a move calls nothing and says
+nothing, and the grid warns once.
+
+```tsx
+const [orders, setOrders] = useState(initial);
+
+<DataGrid
+  data={orders}
+  rowKey="id"
+  columns={columns}
+  caption="Orders"
+  rowReorder
+  onRowReorder={(from, to, position) =>
+    setOrders((rows) => {
+      const moved = rows.find((row) => row.id === from)!;
+      const others = rows.filter((row) => row.id !== from);
+      const at = others.findIndex((row) => row.id === to) + (position === 'after' ? 1 : 0);
+      return [...others.slice(0, at), moved, ...others.slice(at)];
+    })
+  }
+/>;
+```
+
+<Canvas of={GroupingStories.RowReorderDragging} />
+
+**The handle** is a button of 20px by 24px, with the six dots of the Dialog's grip in the muted text
+colour; it is the text colour under the pointer and the accent while its row is dragged. It is the one
+control of its cell, as the box is in the column of boxes, so it has the focus and is the Tab stop
+while its cell is the active one. It is named `labels.reorderRow(name)` ("Reorder DH-1024"), where
+`name` is the text of the row header column, or the key when there is none, and it says
+`aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded` while its menu is open. The title of the column has the
+hidden words `labels.reorderColumn` and is a place of the keyboard with no control.
+
+**While the grid sorts or groups the handles do nothing**, since the order of the rows is then not the
+rows' own: they are `aria-disabled` and dimmed to half, they start no drag and open no menu, and a
+tooltip says why (`labels.reorderDisabled`), on hover and on focus; the handle stays focusable so that
+a keyboard user finds the reason too, and the tooltip is its description. A filter does not turn them
+off.
+
+- **Drag the handle.** With a mouse, a pen or a finger (the handle has `touch-action: none` and is
+  only for this). The row is dimmed to 35% while it is dragged (and its detail, while it is open), a chip
+  with its name follows the pointer, and a line of 3px with a dot at its left end shows where it would
+  go: across what the frame shows, at the boundary before the row under the pointer when the pointer is in
+  its upper half and after it when it is in its lower half (after its detail while that is open). There
+  is no line, and a drop does nothing, beside the row itself, over the heading or the footer, outside
+  the rows and where the boundary is out of sight. The cursor is `grabbing` over the whole page until
+  the pointer is let go. A grid with a `height` scrolls its rows when the pointer is within 40px of the
+  frame's edge, and the page is not scrolled; a virtual grid reads the rows under the pointer from what
+  it has drawn, and a row that left the window is no target, though the row that is dragged may.
+  <Kbd keys="esc" />, `pointercancel`, a lost capture, the grid going and `rowReorder` turning off
+  all end the drag and call nothing, and each takes off what the drag set: the dim, the chip, the
+  line, the cursor, the scroll. `onRowReorder` is called once, at the drop, with the row under the
+  line; the rows are drawn when the drag starts and when it ends (the source row only), and not for
+  a move of the pointer.
+- **The menu.** A press on the handle, <Kbd keys="enter" /> or <Kbd keys="space" /> on it opens the one
+  menu of the grid, under the handle, with Move up, Move down, Move to top and Move to bottom
+  (`labels.moveUp`, `moveDown`, `moveToTop`, `moveToBottom`). An item that would not move the row (up and
+  top for the first row, down and bottom for the last, among the rows after the filter) is off. Choosing
+  one makes the move and closes the menu, and the focus goes back to the handle of the row. The menu
+  closes, for good, when `rowReorder` turns off, when the grid starts to sort or group, and when its row
+  leaves the rows shown. <Kbd keys="space" /> is the button's: the browser presses it when the key is let
+  go, and the key chooses no row.
+- **Keys.** <Kbd keys="mod+shift+up" /> and <Kbd keys="mod+shift+down" /> on any cell of a row, the
+  handle included, move it one place: up is before the row above and down is after the row below. At
+  an edge the key does nothing, and it is cancelled all the same. While the grid sorts or groups it does
+  nothing but say `labels.reorderDisabled`, once for a press.
+- **What is said.** Every move, by the menu, the keys or a drop, is said at once (`labels.announceRowMoved`),
+  with the place the row was asked for among the rows after the filter and how many there are, before
+  your app has answered. A move that nothing keeps (no `onRowReorder`) says nothing.
+
+**The focus follows the row.** The active place is the row's key, so it goes with the row when your app
+moves it, and the focus stays on the cell it was on. When a move by the menu or the keys puts the row on
+another page, the grid goes to that page once, at the first commit where the new `data` shows the rows in
+the order that was asked for, scrolls the row into view the least it takes, and gives the place and the
+focus back to it. That commit ends the request, whatever it shows: a `data` that you changed another way
+is not this move's, and a move that your app never answers waits for no timer. A drop is not followed:
+the pointer is on the row already.
+
+**Pages and server mode.** In a grid with pages a move by the menu or the keys counts over every page,
+and a drag counts over the page shown. In server mode `data` is the page, so every move is within it: the
+keys and the menu stop at the edges of the page, and `onRowReorder` says the keys of rows of that page.
+

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/engine/row-reorder.ts b/src/components/data-grid/engine/row-reorder.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..6a1e3af
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/engine/row-reorder.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+import type { DataGridKey, DataGridRowDrop } from '../types';
+
+/** The four moves of the row menu, and what a key does with `up` and `down`. */
+export type RowMove = 'up' | 'down' | 'top' | 'bottom';
+
+/** What a move asks of the app: the row it goes to, and which side of it. */
+export interface RowAsk {
+  toKey: DataGridKey;
+  position: DataGridRowDrop;
+}
+
+/**
+ * What a move of a row asks, worked out over the keys of the rows after the filter in the order shown
+ * (`keyed`): up is before the row above, down after the row below, top before the first and bottom after
+ * the last (spec phase 6 §6.3). `null` at an edge, where the row cannot go that way, and for a key that is
+ * not among them. The one rule for the keys, the menu and which of its items are turned off.
+ */
+export function askOfMove(
+  keys: readonly DataGridKey[],
+  key: DataGridKey,
+  move: RowMove,
+): RowAsk | null {
+  const at = keys.findIndex((one) => Object.is(one, key));
+  if (at < 0) return null;
+  const last = keys.length - 1;
+  switch (move) {
+    case 'up':
+      return at > 0 ? { toKey: keys[at - 1]!, position: 'before' } : null;
+    case 'down':
+      return at < last ? { toKey: keys[at + 1]!, position: 'after' } : null;
+    case 'top':
+      return at > 0 ? { toKey: keys[0]!, position: 'before' } : null;
+    case 'bottom':
+      return at < last ? { toKey: keys[last]!, position: 'after' } : null;
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * The place, counted from 1, that the row `key` has among `keys` once it has been moved as `ask` says; `0`
+ * when it does not move (the row is not there, or `toKey` is the row itself).
+ */
+export function placeAfterMove(
+  keys: readonly DataGridKey[],
+  key: DataGridKey,
+  ask: RowAsk,
+): number {
+  if (Object.is(key, ask.toKey)) return 0;
+  const others = keys.filter((one) => !Object.is(one, key));
+  const to = others.findIndex((one) => Object.is(one, ask.toKey));
+  if (to < 0 || others.length === keys.length) return 0;
+  return to + (ask.position === 'after' ? 2 : 1);
+}
+

+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import { pagePlaces, rowDrop } from '../engine/row-reorder';
+import type { RowAsk, RowDrop } from '../engine/row-reorder';
+import { markDragCursor, rowBlocks } from '../grid-dom';
+import type { DataGridKey } from '../types';
+import type { DragViewStore } from './use-drag-view';
+
+export interface RowDragOptions<TRow> {
+  /** Whether a drag may start and go on: the grid reorders rows and neither sorts nor groups. */
+  enabled: boolean;
+  frameRef: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;
+  tableRef: RefObject<HTMLTableElement | null>;
+  /** The rows of the page, the three kinds of them. */
+  rows: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[];
+  /** Whether the frame has a height and so scrolls its rows: only then does a drag scroll it. */
+  scrolls: boolean;
+  view: DragViewStore;
+  /** The row's header text, else its key. */
+  nameOf: (row: unknown, key: DataGridKey) => string;
+  /** Tells the app where the row was dropped, with the sentence. */
+  drop: (key: DataGridKey, ask: RowAsk) => void;
+}
+
+export interface RowDrag {
+  /** The press on the handle of the row `key`: the start of a drag, once the pointer has gone past the threshold. */
+  onPointerDown: (event: ReactPointerEvent<HTMLElement>, key: DataGridKey) => void;
+}
+
+/** A drag from its first move to its end. */
+interface Session {
+  key: DataGridKey;
+  name: string;
+  doc: Document;
+  frame: HTMLElement;
+  table: HTMLTableElement;
+  /** Where the pointer was last, for the work that a scroll of the frame does again. */
+  x: number;
+  y: number;
+  autoScroll: AutoScroll | null;
+  onScroll: () => void;
+}
+
+/**
+ * What the frame shows of its rows, vertically: under the sticky heading and above the footer that
+ * sticks, or the bottom of the frame. A boundary outside it is out of sight, and no drop goes there.
+ */
+function visibleBand(frame: HTMLElement, table: HTMLTableElement): { top: number; bottom: number } {
+  const box = frame.getBoundingClientRect();
+  const top = box.top + frame.clientTop;
+  const bottom = top + frame.clientHeight;
+  const head = table.tHead?.getBoundingClientRect().bottom ?? top;
+  const foot = table.tFoot?.getBoundingClientRect().top ?? bottom;
+  return { top: Math.max(top, head), bottom: Math.min(bottom, foot) };
+}
+
+/**
+ * Dragging a row by its handle (spec phase 6 §3.8, §4.3 R1 "Kéo dòng"; every pointer type, a finger
+ * too, since the handle has `touch-action: none` and is only for this). One `usePointerDrag` serves
+ * every handle; the press that starts it names the row, and the `mousedown` of that press is cancelled
+ * by the handle, never the `pointerdown`.
+ *
+ * While the drag is in flight the pointer goes into the store the chip and the line read, so a move
+ * draws no row; the body reads one change at the start and one at the end (the source row is dimmed).
+ * The row under the pointer is read from the DOM at each move (a virtual window has drawn only some
+ * rows, and a row that left it is no target), its half says before or after it, and the line is drawn
+ * at the boundary only where a drop would move the row: not beside the row, not outside the rows, not
+ * under the heading or the footer. The place of the row counts, not whether it is drawn, so a drag may
+ * scroll past it. A frame with a height scrolls under a pointer near its edge, and the boundaries are
+ * measured again after each scroll.
+ *
+ * A release tells the app once, where the line was; Escape, `pointercancel`, a lost capture, the grid
+ * going and the feature being turned off (`enabled`) end the drag and tell nobody. Each end takes off what
+ * the drag set: the cursor mark, the scroll listener, the auto-scroll, the store. Everything the handlers
+ * read comes from the latest commit, so they are the same functions for as long as the grid lives.
+ */
+export function useRowDrag<TRow>(options: RowDragOptions<TRow>): RowDrag {
+  const latest = useRef(options);
+  const places = useMemo(
+    () => (options.enabled ? pagePlaces(options.rows) : new Map<DataGridKey, number>()),
+    [options.enabled, options.rows],
+  );
+  const latestPlaces = useRef(places);
+  useWriteOnCommit(() => {
+    latest.current = options;
+    latestPlaces.current = places;
+  });
+  const pressed = useRef<DataGridKey | null>(null);
+  const session = useRef<Session | null>(null);
+
+  /** Where a drop at the pointer's place would go now, `null` where it would move nothing. */
+  const dropAt = useCallback((current: Session, x: number, y: number): RowDrop | null => {
+    const { rows } = latest.current;
+    const from = latestPlaces.current.get(current.key);
+    if (from === undefined) return null;
+    const box = current.frame.getBoundingClientRect();
+    const left = box.left + current.frame.clientLeft;
+    if (x < left || x > left + current.frame.clientWidth) return null;
+    const band = visibleBand(current.frame, current.table);
+    if (y < band.top || y > band.bottom) return null;
+    const blocks = rowBlocks(current.table, (index) => {
+      const row = rows[index];
+      return row?.kind === 'data' ? row.key : undefined;
+    }).flatMap((block) => {
+      const place = latestPlaces.current.get(block.key);
+      return place === undefined ? [] : [{ ...block, place }];
+    });
+    const found = rowDrop(blocks, from, y);
+    // A boundary that is out of sight (half of a row under the heading) is no place to drop.
+    return found && found.y >= band.top - 0.5 && found.y <= band.bottom + 0.5 ? found : null;
+  }, []);
+
+  const apply = useCallback(
+    (current: Session, x: number, y: number) => {
+      current.x = x;
+      current.y = y;
+      latest.current.view.set({
+        caption: current.name,
+        x,
+        y,
+        edge: dropAt(current, x, y)?.y ?? null,
+        axis: 'y',
+        target: null,
+        slot: null,
+        chip: null,
+        row: current.key,
+      });
+    },
+    [dropAt],
+  );
+
+  // Everything a drag set, taken off: the one place that does it, for each way a drag ends.
+  const settle = useCallback((current: Session) => {
+    current.autoScroll?.stop();
+    current.frame.removeEventListener('scroll', current.onScroll);
+    markDragCursor(current.doc, null);
+    latest.current.view.set(null);
+  }, []);
+
+  const finish = useCallback(
+    (done: boolean) => {
+      const current = session.current;
+      if (!current) return;
+      session.current = null;
+      // The rows may have changed while the button was held: the drop is worked out again from them.
+      const found = done && latest.current.enabled ? dropAt(current, current.x, current.y) : null;
+      settle(current);
+      if (found) latest.current.drop(current.key, found.ask);
+    },
+    [dropAt, settle],
+  );
+
+  const drag = usePointerDrag({
+    onStart: ({ x, y }) => {
+      const key = pressed.current;
+      const { enabled, frameRef, tableRef, rows, scrolls, nameOf } = latest.current;
+      const frame = frameRef.current;
+      const table = tableRef.current;
+      if (key === null || !enabled || !frame || !table) return;
+      const row = rows.find((one) => one.kind === 'data' && Object.is(one.key, key));
+      if (!row) return;
+      const next: Session = {
+        key,
+        name: nameOf(row.kind === 'data' ? row.row : undefined, key),
+        doc: frame.ownerDocument,
+        frame,
+        table,
+        x,
+        y,
+        autoScroll: scrolls
+          ? createAutoScroll(frame, {
+              axis: 'y',
+              area: () => ({ left: 0, right: 0, ...visibleBand(frame, table) }),
+            })
+          : null,
+        // The frame scrolls under a pointer that rests: the boundaries are somewhere else now.
+        onScroll: () => apply(next, next.x, next.y),
+      };
+      session.current = next;
+      frame.addEventListener('scroll', next.onScroll, { passive: true });
+      markDragCursor(next.doc, 'grabbing');
+    },
+    onMove: ({ x, y }) => {
+      const current = session.current;
+      if (!current) return;
+      apply(current, x, y);
+      current.autoScroll?.update(x, y);
+    },
+    onEnd: () => finish(true),
+    onCancel: () => finish(false),
+  });
+
+  // The feature turned off (or the grid starting to sort or group) in the middle of a drag takes the drag
+  // with it, and so does the grid going.
+  const { enabled } = options;
+  useEffect(() => {
+    if (!enabled) finish(false);
+  }, [enabled, finish]);
+  useEffect(
+    () => () => {
+      const current = session.current;
+      session.current = null;
+      if (current) settle(current);
+    },
+    [settle],
+  );
+
+  const { onPointerDown: startDrag } = drag;
+  const onPointerDown = useCallback(
+    (event: ReactPointerEvent<HTMLElement>, key: DataGridKey) => {
+      pressed.current = key;
+      startDrag(event);
+    },
+    [startDrag],
+  );
+  return useMemo(() => ({ onPointerDown }), [onPointerDown]);
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-menu.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-menu.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bdf13bd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-menu.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+import { useCallback, useMemo } from 'react';
+import type { FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import type { DataGridKey } from '../types';
+import { useAnchoredOpen } from './use-anchored-open';
+import type { AnchoredOpen, AnchoredView } from './use-anchored-open';
+import { useIsoLayoutEffect } from '../../../internal/use-iso-layout-effect';
+
+/** What the one row menu of the grid is about: the row, its name, and the handle it opens under. */
+export interface RowMenuView extends AnchoredView {
+  readonly key: DataGridKey;
+  /** The row's header text, else its key: what the menu is named after. */
+  readonly name: string;
+}
+
+export interface RowMenuControl {
+  store: AnchoredOpen<RowMenuView>['store'];
+  /** Opens the menu of the row with this key, named `name`, under its handle. */
+  open: (key: DataGridKey, name: string, from: HTMLElement) => void;
+  close: () => void;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The one menu of the rows of a grid (spec phase 6 §3.6, §6.3): its state, which only the handles and the
+ * menu read, so opening and closing it draws no row. A popup dies with what opened it (PR #44 5): it closes,
+ * for good, when `rowReorder` turns off, when the grid starts to sort or group (`enabled` is whether the
+ * handles can move a row now), and when its row leaves the rows shown.
+ */
+export function useRowMenu<TRow>({
+  enabled,
+  rows,
+}: {
+  enabled: boolean;
+  rows: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[];
+}): RowMenuControl {
+  const { store, open: openAt, close } = useAnchoredOpen<RowMenuView>();
+  const open = useCallback(
+    (key: DataGridKey, name: string, from: HTMLElement) => openAt({ key, name, from }),
+    [openAt],
+  );
+  useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
+    const view = store.get();
+    if (!view?.open) return;
+    if (!enabled || !rows.some((row) => row.kind === 'data' && Object.is(row.key, view.key))) {
+      close();
+    }
+  });
+  return useMemo(() => ({ store, open, close }), [store, open, close]);
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-reorder.ts b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-reorder.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..09cb759
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/hooks/use-row-reorder.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,155 @@
+import { useCallback, useMemo, useRef } from 'react';
+import { useIsoLayoutEffect } from '../../../internal/use-iso-layout-effect';
+import { useWriteOnCommit } from '../../../internal/use-write-on-commit';
+import type { ResolvedColumn } from '../engine/columns';
+import type { FlatDataRow, FlatRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import { askOfMove, isPlacedAs, placeAfterMove } from '../engine/row-reorder';
+import type { RowAsk, RowMove } from '../engine/row-reorder';
+import type { DataGridKey, DataGridLabels, DataGridRowDrop } from '../types';
+
+export interface RowReorderOptions<TRow> {
+  /** Whether the grid reorders rows (`rowReorder`). */
+  enabled: boolean;
+  /** Whether the grid sorts or groups now: the handles and the keys do nothing but say why. */
+  off: boolean;
+  /** Every data row after the filter, in the order shown: the rows a move is counted among. */
+  keyed: readonly FlatDataRow<TRow>[];
+  /** The rows the app gave, which the move waits for a change of. */
+  data: readonly TRow[];
+  /** The column whose text names a row (the row header). */
+  rowHeader: ResolvedColumn<TRow> | undefined;
+  textOf: (row: TRow, column: ResolvedColumn<TRow>) => string;
+  onRowReorder:
+    ((from: DataGridKey, to: DataGridKey, position: DataGridRowDrop) => void) | undefined;
+  labels: DataGridLabels;
+  announce: (text: string) => void;
+  /** The handle's `scrollToRow`: its page, then the row scrolled into view the least it takes. */
+  scrollToRow: (key: DataGridKey) => boolean;
+  /** The rows of the page shown: a row that left it has lost the place of the keyboard to its neighbour. */
+  rows: readonly FlatRow<TRow>[];
+  /** Puts the active place on the row with this key, and the focus there when the grid has it. */
+  focusRow: (key: DataGridKey) => void;
+}
+
+export interface RowReorder {
+  /** The keys of the rows after the filter, in the order shown; none while the grid does not reorder. */
+  keys: readonly DataGridKey[];
+  /** The row's header text, else its key: what the handle, the menu and the sentences call it. */
+  nameOf: (row: unknown, key: DataGridKey) => string;
+  /** A move of the menu or of the keys: the row follows the app's answer to its page and into sight. */
+  move: (key: DataGridKey, how: RowMove) => void;
+  /** A move by `mod+Shift+↑` or `↓`; while the grid sorts or groups it says why, once for a press. */
+  moveByKey: (key: DataGridKey, step: -1 | 1, repeat: boolean) => void;
+  /** A drop of the pointer: the line has said where, and the row is not followed (it is under the pointer). */
+  drop: (key: DataGridKey, ask: RowAsk) => void;
+}
+
+const NO_KEYS: readonly DataGridKey[] = [];
+
+/** A move waiting for the app's answer: the `data` it was asked of, which the answer is a change of. */
+interface Pending {
+  key: DataGridKey;
+  ask: RowAsk;
+  data: readonly unknown[];
+}
+
+/**
+ * What the user does to the order of the rows (spec phase 6 §3.6, §6.3): the three ways to ask for a move
+ * (the menu, the keys, a drop) are one function, which tells `onRowReorder` once with the row it goes to and
+ * which side, and says where the row went, among the rows after the filter, before the app has answered. The
+ * grid moves nothing: the app changes `data`.
+ *
+ * A move by the menu or the keys is followed. The place of the keyboard is by key, so it goes with a row
+ * that stays on its page; the page and the sight are this hook's: at the first commit with another `data`
+ * than the one the move was asked of, if the rows are in the order that was asked for, the row is scrolled
+ * to, which goes to its page first when it is on another and then scrolls it into view the least it takes.
+ * A row that left the page left the place with its neighbour (the keyboard does that for any row that goes),
+ * so the commit that shows it on its page gives the place back to it, and the focus when the grid has it.
+ * The first commit ends the request, whatever it shows: a `data` the app changed another way is not this
+ * move's, and one the app never changed leaves it waiting for nothing but a change.
+ */
+export function useRowReorder<TRow>(options: RowReorderOptions<TRow>): RowReorder {
+  const { enabled, keyed, data } = options;
+  const keys = useMemo(() => (enabled ? keyed.map((row) => row.key) : NO_KEYS), [enabled, keyed]);
+  const latest = useRef({ ...options, keys });
+  useWriteOnCommit(() => {
+    latest.current = { ...options, keys };
+  });
+  const pending = useRef<Pending | null>(null);
+
+  const nameOf = useCallback((row: unknown, key: DataGridKey): string => {
+    const { rowHeader, textOf } = latest.current;
+    const text = rowHeader ? textOf(row as TRow, rowHeader) : '';
+    return text === '' ? String(key) : text;
+  }, []);
+
+  const ask = useCallback(
+    (key: DataGridKey, asked: RowAsk, follow: boolean): void => {
+      const {
+        keys: shown,
+        keyed: rows,
+        onRowReorder,
+        labels,
+        announce,
+        data: given,
+      } = latest.current;
+      const place = placeAfterMove(shown, key, asked);
+      if (!onRowReorder || place === 0) return;
+      const row = rows.find((one) => Object.is(one.key, key));
+      onRowReorder(key, asked.toKey, asked.position);
+      announce(labels.announceRowMoved(nameOf(row?.row, key), place, shown.length));
+      pending.current = follow ? { key, ask: asked, data: given } : null;
+    },
+    [nameOf],
+  );
+
+  const move = useCallback(
+    (key: DataGridKey, how: RowMove): void => {
+      const asked = askOfMove(latest.current.keys, key, how);
+      if (asked) ask(key, asked, true);
+    },
+    [ask],
+  );
+
+  const moveByKey = useCallback(
+    (key: DataGridKey, step: -1 | 1, repeat: boolean): void => {
+      const { off, labels, announce } = latest.current;
+      if (off) {
+        if (!repeat) announce(labels.reorderDisabled);
+        return;
+      }
+      move(key, step < 0 ? 'up' : 'down');
+    },
+    [move],
+  );
+
+  const drop = useCallback((key: DataGridKey, asked: RowAsk) => ask(key, asked, false), [ask]);
+
+  // The row that went to another page, waiting to be shown there: the commit after the one that asked for
+  // the page gives it its place back, or finds it is not shown and lets it go. Declared before the effect
+  // that sets it, so the commit that asks does not settle it.
+  const following = useRef<DataGridKey | null>(null);
+  useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
+    const key = following.current;
+    if (key === null) return;
+    following.current = null;
+    const now = latest.current;
+    const shown = now.rows.some((row) => row.kind === 'data' && Object.is(row.key, key));
+    if (now.enabled && shown) now.focusRow(key);
+  });
+  useIsoLayoutEffect(() => {
+    const request = pending.current;
+    if (!request || request.data === data) return;
+    pending.current = null;
+    const now = latest.current;
+    if (!now.enabled || !isPlacedAs(now.keys, request.key, request.ask)) return;
+    const shown = now.rows.some((row) => row.kind === 'data' && Object.is(row.key, request.key));
+    now.scrollToRow(request.key);
+    if (!shown) following.current = request.key;
+  }, [data]);
+
+  return useMemo(
+    () => ({ keys, nameOf, move, moveByKey, drop }),
+    [keys, nameOf, move, moveByKey, drop],
+  );
+}

diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/parts/RowHandle.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/parts/RowHandle.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..5a32a08
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/parts/RowHandle.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+import { useRef, useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';
+import type { MouseEvent } from 'react';
+import { GripIcon } from '../../../internal/icons';
+import { useTriggerPress } from '../../../internal/use-popover-trigger';
+import { TooltipContent, TooltipRoot, TooltipTrigger } from '../../tooltip/Tooltip';
+import type { FlatDataRow } from '../engine/flatten';
+import type { PinPlace } from '../engine/layout';
+import { useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+import { pinAttributes } from './pin-attributes';
+
+/**
+ * The cell of the column of handles in a data row. The handle is the cell's one control (the data grid
+ * pattern of the APG: a cell that holds one simple control gives the focus to it), so it is the Tab stop
+ * when this is the active cell and the cell never is.
+ *
+ * A press on it is a press on the row's handle: the `mousedown` is cancelled and the handle focused (the
+ * drag may begin, and a text selection must not), the pointer goes to the drag, and a click that stays
+ * under the threshold opens the row menu (`useTriggerPress`: a second press on the handle of the open menu
+ * closes it). Enter and Space, which the keyboard turns into that click, open it the same way. While the
+ * grid sorts or groups the handle is `aria-disabled` and does nothing but say why (a tooltip, which is also
+ * its description), and it stays focusable, so that a keyboard user finds the reason too.
+ */
+export function HandleCell<TRow>({
+  flat,
+  isActive,
+  pin,
+}: {
+  flat: FlatDataRow<TRow>;
+  isActive: boolean;
+  pin: PinPlace | undefined;
+}) {
+  const { labels, rowHeader, textOf, rowReorder } = useGridContext<TRow>();
+  const reorder = rowReorder!;
+  const { menu, off } = reorder;
+  const text = rowHeader ? textOf(flat.row, rowHeader) : '';
+  const name = text === '' ? String(flat.key) : text;
+  // Whether the menu is open for this row: a boolean, so opening or closing it draws this cell only when it
+  // is the row's, and never the others.
+  const open = useSyncExternalStore(
+    menu.store.subscribe,
+    () => {
+      const view = menu.store.get();
+      return view?.open === true && Object.is(view.key, flat.key);
+    },
+    () => false,
+  );
+  const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
+  const press = useTriggerPress(open, (wasOpen) => {
+    if (off) return;
+    if (wasOpen) menu.close();
+    else if (buttonRef.current) menu.open(flat.key, name, buttonRef.current);
+  });
+  const onMouseDown = (event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>): void => {
+    if (off || event.button !== 0) return;
+    event.preventDefault();
+    event.currentTarget.focus({ preventScroll: true });
+  };
+  const handle = (
+    <button
+      ref={buttonRef}
+      type="button"
+      className="flg-data-grid-row-handle"
+      aria-label={labels.reorderRow(name)}
+      aria-haspopup="menu"
+      aria-expanded={open}
+      aria-controls={open ? reorder.contentId : undefined}
+      aria-disabled={off ? true : undefined}
+      tabIndex={isActive ? 0 : -1}
+      onPointerDown={(event) => {
+        if (off) return;
+        press.onPointerDown();
+        reorder.onPointerDown(event, flat.key);
+      }}
+      onPointerCancel={press.onPointerCancel}
+      onMouseDown={onMouseDown}
+      onClick={press.onClick}
+    >
+      <GripIcon width={8} height={14} aria-hidden="true" />
+    </button>
+  );
+  return (
+    <td
+      className="flg-table-cell flg-data-grid-cell flg-data-grid-handle-cell"
+      data-service="drag"
+      tabIndex={-1}
+      {...pinAttributes(pin)}
+    >
+      {off ? (
+        <TooltipRoot>
+          <TooltipTrigger>{handle}</TooltipTrigger>
+          <TooltipContent side="right" align="center" sideOffset={8}>
+            {labels.reorderDisabled}
+          </TooltipContent>
+        </TooltipRoot>
+      ) : (
+        handle
+      )}
+    </td>
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * The title of the column of handles: a place of the keyboard with no control, and the words
+ * `labels.reorderColumn` hidden in it, which a table header with no name would fail an accessibility check
+ * without.
+ */
+export function HandleHead({ isActive, pin }: { isActive: boolean; pin: PinPlace | undefined }) {
+  const { labels } = useGridContext();
+  return (
+    <th
+      scope="col"
+      className="flg-table-head flg-data-grid-head"
+      data-service="drag"
+      tabIndex={isActive ? 0 : -1}
+      {...pinAttributes(pin)}
+    >
+      <span className="flg-visually-hidden">{labels.reorderColumn}</span>
+    </th>
+  );
+}
diff --git a/src/components/data-grid/parts/RowMenu.tsx b/src/components/data-grid/parts/RowMenu.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..4689082
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/components/data-grid/parts/RowMenu.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+import { useMemo } from 'react';
+import type { MutableRefObject, ReactNode } from 'react';
+import { ArrowIcon, ChevronIcon } from '../../../internal/icons';
+import { MenuTreeContext } from '../../menu/menu-context';
+import type { FocusOnOpen } from '../../menu/menu-context';
+import { MenuItem } from '../../menu/Menu';
+import { MenuPanel } from '../../menu/MenuPanel';
+import { askOfMove } from '../engine/row-reorder';
+import type { RowMove } from '../engine/row-reorder';
+import { useGridContext } from '../grid-context';
+import { useExternalStore } from '../hooks/use-external-store';
+import type { RowMenuControl } from '../hooks/use-row-menu';
+import type { DataGridKey } from '../types';
+
+// The menu opens on its first item, whichever way it was asked for.
+const FIRST: MutableRefObject<FocusOnOpen> = { current: 'first' };
+
+const ITEMS: readonly { move: RowMove; icon: ReactNode }[] = [
+  { move: 'up', icon: <ArrowIcon direction="up" /> },
+  { move: 'down', icon: <ArrowIcon direction="down" /> },
+  { move: 'top', icon: <ChevronIcon direction="up" /> },
+  { move: 'bottom', icon: <ChevronIcon direction="down" /> },
+];
+
+/**
+ * The one menu of the grid's rows (spec phase 6 §3.6, §6.3), the menu of the library (`MenuPanel`) as
+ * `ColumnMenu` composes it, after the frame and outside the table. It opens under the handle of a row with
+ * four items, Move up, Move down, Move to top and Move to bottom; the ones that would not move the row (at
+ * an edge of the rows after the filter) are turned off. Choosing one moves the row as the keys do and
+ * closes the menu, and the focus goes where the active cell's home is (`restoreFocusTo`), read after the
+ * commit: the handle of the row, which the active place follows by its key.
+ */
+export function RowMenu({
+  menu,
+  keys,
+  move,
+  restoreFocusTo,
+}: {
+  menu: RowMenuControl;
+  /** The keys of the rows after the filter, in the order shown. */
+  keys: readonly DataGridKey[];
+  move: (key: DataGridKey, how: RowMove) => void;
+  restoreFocusTo: () => HTMLElement | null;
+}) {
+  const { labels, rowReorder } = useGridContext();
+  const view = useExternalStore(menu.store);
+  const tree = useMemo(() => ({ closeAll: menu.close }), [menu.close]);
+  const words: Record<RowMove, string> = {
+    up: labels.moveUp,
+    down: labels.moveDown,
+    top: labels.moveToTop,
+    bottom: labels.moveToBottom,
+  };
+  return (
+    <MenuTreeContext.Provider value={tree}>
+      <MenuPanel
+        className="flg-data-grid-row-menu"
+        aria-label={view ? labels.reorderRow(view.name) : undefined}
+        open={view?.open === true}
+        report={(open) => {
+          if (!open) menu.close();
+        }}
+        contentId={rowReorder?.contentId ?? ''}
+        reference={() => view?.from ?? null}
+        restoreFocusTo={restoreFocusTo}
+        focusOnOpen={FIRST}
+        side="bottom"
+        align="start"
+        offset={4}
+      >
+        {view
+          ? ITEMS.map(({ move: how, icon }) => (
+              <MenuItem
+                key={how}
+                icon={icon}
+                disabled={askOfMove(keys, view.key, how) === null}
+                onSelect={() => move(view.key, how)}
+              >
+                {words[how]}
+              </MenuItem>
+            ))
+          : null}
+      </MenuPanel>
+    </MenuTreeContext.Provider>
+  );
+}

Build, rồi ghi ngưỡng kích thước. Plan không chép `.size-limit.json`: `size:record` tự ghi file đó. `pnpm check:package` chạy sau, vì với ngưỡng cũ bước `size` của nó fail (phát hiện 22):

```bash
pnpm gen:theme
pnpm build
pnpm size:record
pnpm check:package
```

Expected: `size:record` ghi ngưỡng mới gần JS (all exports) 63693 B, JS (DataGrid) 81337 B, CSS 21964 B (trước: 63693 B, 67213 B, 20745 B), là kết quả ở bản nháp; ngưỡng là số đo cộng 10% (số đo ở bản nháp: 57.90 kB, 73.94 kB, 19.97 kB). `.size-limit.json` là file duy nhất lệnh đó đổi. Nếu số khác một chút, giữ số do `size:record` ghi và nêu trong báo cáo. `pnpm check:package`: PASS với ngưỡng mới.

- [ ] **Step 4: Chạy kiểm tra**

Kiểm tra cuối của cả nhánh, như Claude chạy trên bản nháp (`check-p6e.sh`), cộng story theo từng thư mục, từng project và từng trình duyệt:

```bash
pnpm gen:theme
pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm format:check
npx tsc --noEmit -p .
pnpm check:name
pnpm check:contrast
pnpm build && pnpm check:package
pnpm size
pnpm vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=3
pnpm vitest run --project unit-react18 --maxWorkers=3
pnpm vitest run --project scripts --maxWorkers=3
pnpm build-storybook
pnpm check:docs-tables
for d in src/components/data-grid src/components/table src/components/search-field src/docs; do
  for b in chromium firefox webkit; do
    pnpm vitest run --project storybook-light --browser=$b $d
    pnpm vitest run --project storybook-dark --browser=$b $d
